notes: Representations and characters are proposed as functors of an unknown field; identities valid over several fields are suggested to hold universally.
statement: An algebraic group can be a functor on fields, but its complex unitary or tracial character theory additionally depends on the topology of its field of points, the category of representations, parameters and normalization. No category, transition maps or transfer principle for the proposed character functor is specified.
reconstruction: No modern transfer theorem or Langlands statement is substituted for the unformalized proposal.
fate: The local formulas compared below and the adelic construction in \citet{gelfand1964adeles} account for the motivation. They do not give a theorem that equality over several fields forces equality over every field.
present_status: As of November 2026: A recognisable research programme with insufficient data for a definite mathematical claim or an open-problem status.

title: Complex rank-one distribution characters
notes: For complex matrices of determinant one the notes write a numerator \(\pi(\lambda)+\pi(\lambda^{-1})\) divided by \(|\lambda-\lambda^{-1}|^2\), attributed to Gelfand and Naimark, 1947.
statement: For the normalized principal series of \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)\) induced by a unitary character \(\chi\) of \(\mathbb C^\times\), its distribution character on a regular semisimple element with eigenvalues \(\lambda,\lambda^{-1}\) is \((\chi(\lambda)+\chi(\lambda^{-1}))/|\lambda-\lambda^{-1}|^2\), with ordinary complex modulus in the denominator. The trace is defined after integration against a test function; it is not an ordinary trace of the individual infinite-dimensional operator.
reconstruction: Normalized induction, the distributional meaning and the regular-semisimple domain are supplied; the 1947 original was not separately opened.
fate: The notebook’s 1947 attribution is consistent with the historical references in \citet{gelfandgraev1963representations}. Its Section 5.1, equation (5), gives the principal-series formula with the local-field absolute value, which for \(\mathbb C\) is the square of ordinary modulus.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established regular-semisimple character formula. Values at the identity or repeated eigenvalues cannot be obtained by substituting directly into this quotient.

title: Real rank-one principal and discrete series
notes: The real principal-series expression vanishes for nonreal eigenvalues. A second expression, apparently for a discrete-series family, has an undefined minimum eigenvalue and a row without its condition; the 1947 marginal surname remains unclear.
statement: For a normalized unitary principal series of \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)\) induced from a character \(\chi\) of \(\mathbb R^\times\), the regular character is \((\chi(\lambda)+\chi(\lambda^{-1}))/|\lambda-\lambda^{-1}|\) on split semisimple elements and zero on elliptic regular elements. The discrete series are additional representations. For a holomorphic discrete series with lowest rotation weight \(k\ge2\), one compatible elliptic boundary-value convention gives \(e^{ik\theta}/(1-e^{2i\theta})\) for \(\theta\notin\pi\mathbb Z\); changing the rotation convention conjugates or reverses this formula.
reconstruction: The distinction between the two families and the displayed rotation-weight convention are editorial. The uncertain surname is retained rather than silently replaced with Bargmann.
fate: The principal-series formula is the real specialization of \citet[Section 5.1, equation (5)]{gelfandgraev1963representations}. The discrete-series expression is an explicit modern highest/lowest-weight reconstruction from the geometric series of rotation weights, not a claimed decipherment of the incomplete second brace.
present_status: As of November 2026: The representation families and distribution characters are established. The source’s second formula and marginal author cannot be uniquely identified at the same confidence as the principal-series line.

title: Non-Archimedean principal-series characters
notes: The same quotient is written for a p-adic field, zero when the eigenvalue is not in the base field, and attributed to Gelfand and Graev, 1963.
statement: Let \(K\) be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero and odd residue characteristic, and let \(\chi\) be a unitary character of \(K^\times\). The normalized induced principal-series character on a regular split semisimple element of \(\mathrm{SL}_2(K)\), with eigenvalues \(\lambda,\lambda^{-1}\), is \((\chi(\lambda)+\chi(\lambda^{-1}))/|\lambda-\lambda^{-1}|_K\); it is zero on regular elliptic elements. At reducibility parameters this is the character of the entire induced representation, not automatically of either irreducible constituent.
reconstruction: The normalized local absolute value and the distinction between induced and irreducible characters remove hidden conventions; the chosen field range stays within the opened source.
fate: Exact source match: \citet[Section 5.1, equation (5)]{gelfandgraev1963representations}, received 8 April 1963 and published in the 1963 survey. The formula and its regularity qualifications were read.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established principal-series formula. Supercuspidal and other discrete-series characters are not exhausted by this one line.

title: Finite-field split and nonsplit character formulae
notes: For a finite field, the split formula loses its denominator, and another family has \(-\pi(\lambda)-\pi(\lambda^{-1})\) on nonsplit elements. The margin says Frobenius, 1895.
statement: For odd \(q\), a generic principal-series character of \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_q)\), induced from \(\chi:\mathbb F_q^\times\to\mathbb C^\times\) with \(\chi^2\ne1\), has value \(\chi(\lambda)+\chi(\lambda^{-1})\) on regular split elements and zero on regular nonsplit elements. A generic cuspidal character associated with a character \(\theta\) of the norm-one torus in \(\mathbb F_{q^2}^\times\), \(\theta^2\ne1\), is zero on regular split elements and \(-\theta(\lambda)-\theta(\lambda^{-1})\) on regular nonsplit elements. Central, unipotent and exceptional parameters require further rows.
reconstruction: The two parameter groups differ: the nonsplit parameter belongs to the norm-one torus, not to the multiplicative group of the base field.
fate: The formula is read in \citet[Sections 2.5 and 3.6, especially Exercise 3.44 and Lemma 3.45]{prasad2007representations}, whose construction supplies a modern verification. Its introduction dates the complete finite-group classifications to Jordan and Schur in 1907, so the notebook’s bare Frobenius 1895 label is not used as a verified exact publication citation.
present_status: As of November 2026: The finite character theory is established. The two displayed families are not a complete character table without their exceptional and nonregular cases.

title: Trace as a proposed conjugacy coordinate
notes: For a determinant-one matrix, the notes say the conjugacy class is determined by \(\alpha+\delta\).
statement: Over an algebraically closed field, a regular semisimple \(\mathrm{SL}_2\) conjugacy class is determined by its trace. Without regularity, the identity and a nontrivial unipotent matrix both have trace two but are not conjugate. Over a nonclosed field, a stable conjugacy class can split into several rational conjugacy classes, so trace alone is not a universal coordinate.
reconstruction: The regularity and field restrictions are mathematical corrections, not changes to the visible handwriting.
fate: The explicit split, elliptic, central and unipotent distinctions in \citet[Section 2.4]{prasad2007representations} and \citet[Section 5]{gelfandgraev1963representations} show the missing domain of the notebook assertion.
present_status: As of November 2026: The unqualified assertion is false; it is a valid coordinate on the specified regular semisimple algebraically closed setting.

title: Adeles as a framework for local-field analogies
notes: Adeles are described as a direct sum of all p-adic groups, with the rational numbers as the diagonal.
statement: The adele ring of \(\mathbb Q\) is \(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb R\times\prod_p'\mathbb Q_p\), restricted relative to \(\mathbb Z_p\): all but finitely many finite coordinates are integral, not necessarily zero. The diagonal \(\mathbb Q\) is discrete and cocompact in this full additive adele group. Omitting the real place gives finite adeles, in which \(\mathbb Q\) is dense rather than discrete.
reconstruction: Restricted product and the Archimedean place replace the shorthand direct-sum description; additive cocompactness is the standard specialization to \(\mathbb G_a\).
fate: \citet[Section 1, p. 487]{gelfand1964adeles}, received 8 January 1964 and published before the talk, explicitly uses all inequivalent valuations and the restricted-product condition for adelic matrix groups. The definition and diagonal-subgroup statement were read.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established local-to-global framework. The literal algebraic direct sum cannot contain the proposed nonzero rational diagonal.

title: Admissible integers represented by three squares
notes: The problem asks which \(m\) are sums of three squares and notes the obstruction \(m=8a+7\).
statement: A positive integer \(m\) is represented by three integral squares exactly when \(m\ne4^a(8b+7)\) for nonnegative integers \(a,b\). The visible mod-eight obstruction is necessary but is only one stage of the complete criterion, since divisibility by four forces all three coordinates even.
reconstruction: The full obstruction and the powers-of-four countersequence supplement the source’s single congruence example.
fate: This classical criterion predates the seminar and provides the arithmetic background to \citet[Section 1]{linnik1957sphere}; a checked modern discussion appears in \citet[Section 1]{ellenberg2010linnik}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established existence criterion. Existence alone does not imply equidistribution as the radius grows: multiplying a fixed radius squared by powers of four preserves the finite set of directions.

title: Linnik angular equidistribution with a fixed splitting prime
notes: The proportion of lattice points projecting into a region is said to approach its area when \(\xi^2+m\equiv0\pmod q\) is solvable for a fixed prime \(q\).
statement: Fix a prime \(q>3\). Let \(m\to\infty\) through integers congruent to \(1,2,3,5,6\pmod8\) and satisfying the Legendre-symbol condition \(\bigl(\frac{-m}{q}\bigr)=1\). For a fixed region \(\Omega\subset S^2\) with piecewise smooth boundary, the proportion of points \(x\in\mathbb Z^3\), \(|x|^2=m\), for which \(x/\sqrt m\in\Omega\), tends to \(\operatorname{area}(\Omega)/(4\pi)\). The analogous statement holds for primitive points. Requiring Legendre symbol one also excludes \(q\mid m\), so mere solvability with the zero residue is weaker.
reconstruction: The admissible congruence classes, fixed prime, nonzero square condition, normalized area and limit are supplied from the original theorem.
fate: Exact prior match: \citet[Theorem 1, Section 2, p. 258]{linnik1957sphere}, received 11 July 1956 and published 1957. The paper distinguishes all and primitive points in equations (2.1)--(2.2). \citet[pp. 73--74]{duke1988hyperbolic} later removes the fixed splitting-prime restriction by modular-form methods.
present_status: As of November 2026: The stated theorem is established. In particular, for squarefree admissible \(m\), Duke’s 1988 result gives equidistribution without a fixed splitting prime. No unrestricted assertion along \(m=4^a m_0\) follows.

title: Arithmetic dynamics from rational orthogonal matrices
notes: Matrices with entries \(a/q\) are used to move integral sphere points; the note says each point has its own 48 orthogonal matrices, then calls the evolution a Markov chain.
statement: Under the splitting condition, Linnik constructs arithmetic trajectories using rational orthogonal transformations with prime-power denominators, after passing to a fundamental region for the finite integral symmetry group. Choosing a root of \(c^2+m\equiv0\pmod{q^k}\) selects one of two directions in the reduced dynamics. Equidistribution requires arithmetic control of long trajectories and their correlations; it does not follow solely from calling a finite evolution a Markov chain.
reconstruction: The distinction between a deterministic reduced trajectory, integral symmetries and a Markov presentation prevents an unsupported identification of the number 48.
fate: \citet[Section 3, pp. 258--260, Theorems 3--4]{linnik1957sphere} gives the deterministic reduced flow and its ergodic/mixing statements. \citet[Sections 2, 8 and 9]{ellenberg2010linnik} develops a graph and random-walk formulation. Neither read source identifies the notebook’s unexplained 48 as a universal transition degree for each prime.
present_status: As of November 2026: The arithmetic method is established and has later graph-theoretic refinements. The written 48 is retained as an unresolved combinatorial shorthand: the full integral orthogonal symmetry group has order 48, but this fact does not establish that the manuscript means precisely that group.

title: Stability of the Fredholm index
notes: The notes set \(k=\dim\ker T\), \(\ell=\dim\operatorname{coker}K\), \(\text{\ae}=k-\ell\), unchanged by small or completely continuous perturbations.
statement: For a bounded Fredholm \(T:X\to Y\) between Banach spaces, the index is locally constant in operator norm and unchanged by addition of a compact operator.
reconstruction: Banach spaces, boundedness and norm topology are supplied; the isolated K is normalized to T.
fate: The background is explicitly recalled by \citet[p.~861, Theorem~1.1]{smale1965sard}; the elliptic setting already appears in \citet[p.~423]{atiyahsinger1963index}.
present_status: As of November 2026, both invariance assertions hold with Fredholmness, closed range, and a fixed topology.

title: What the integer index classifies
notes: Vishik considers index the only homotopy invariant.
statement: For infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert \(H\), the path components of the norm-topological \(\operatorname{Fred}(H)\) are classified by the integer index. For compact Hausdorff \(X\), families instead satisfy \([X,\operatorname{Fred}(H)]\cong K^0(X)\).
reconstruction: Ambient Hilbert space and topology supplied.
fate: \citet[pp.~129--142]{janich1965fredholm}, published April 1965, gives the precise family formulation. The notebook does not specify the intended ambient space.
present_status: As of November 2026, the component statement is true in the full Fredholm space; it does not classify restricted elliptic symbols or all families.

title: Index for nonlinear elliptic maps
notes: What are kernel, cokernel and index for a nonlinear equation? Linearize at every point.
statement: A \(C^1\) map \(F:M\to N\) of Banach manifolds is Fredholm if every \(DF_x\) is Fredholm. Its derivative index is locally constant, hence constant on connected \(M\). This does not define vector-space kernels or cokernels for \(F\) itself.
reconstruction: The Banach-manifold and Fredholm-derivative assumptions are supplied.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.3 and Section~2]{smale1965sard} gives the Fredholm-map framework and elliptic applications. Received 2 November 1964, the day of this seminar, and published October 1965; a causal connection is not established.
present_status: As of November 2026, Fredholm-map theory supplies the precise answer in this framework.

title: Stable invariant of a family
notes: For \(T_x\), \(x\in X\), an invariant of the whole family is sought.
statement: For norm-continuous \(T:X\to\operatorname{Fred}(H)\), with compact Hausdorff \(X\), choose finite-dimensional \(V\) with \(T_xH+V=H\). Then \(E_x=T_x^{-1}V\) is a bundle and \([E]-[X\times V]\in K^0(X)\) is independent of \(V\).
reconstruction: Compactness, continuity and stabilization are supplied.
fate: \citet[pp.~129--142]{janich1965fredholm} identifies the Fredholm classifying space in 1965, giving the family invariant. No transmission from this seminar is claimed.
present_status: As of November 2026, the index bundle answers the stable question; its rank is the numerical index.

title: Statistical-mechanics reading programme
notes: Two or three Ruelle works, one Yang--Lee work, and Kac models are proposed.
statement: A reading programme in rigorous equilibrium statistical mechanics, rather than a theorem.
fate: Ruelle author metadata confirms \citet[pp.~183--197]{ruelle1963classical} and adjacent 1963--64 papers as plausible reading. The unspecified list cannot be uniquely reconstructed.
present_status: As of November 2026, the subject is identifiable but the exact proposed bibliography is not.

title: Confinement of pair-potential minimizers
notes: A repulsive-core/attractive-well graph accompanies a double interaction sum; a minimizing configuration is said to lie in a sphere of radius \(C\). Nearby powers of \(N\) are unclear.
statement: No unique mathematical statement can be extracted: potential hypotheses, treatment of self-interactions, existence, dimension and dependence of \(C\) on particle number are absent.
fate: Povzner/Ruelle, ground-state, confinement and pair-potential searches did not locate this exact statement. Thermodynamic stability alone does not supply it.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fragment remains unidentifiable from the supplied evidence; this does not establish that a mathematical problem is open.

title: Retracted invariant-subspace announcement
notes: \ru{Решено!!!} accompanies a reference to a 1964 Bulletin AMS de Branges paper and a second author, with Livshits mentioned.
statement: The intended question is whether every bounded operator on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space has a closed invariant subspace other than \(0,H\). The de Branges--Rovnyak affirmative announcement was retracted.
reconstruction: Boundedness, complex scalars, separability and closed nontrivial subspace are supplied.
fate: \citet[pp.~718--721]{debrangesrovnyak1964existence} was retracted in \citet[p.~396]{debrangesrovnyak1965correction}. Both publication records and the retraction were checked in the authors’ institutional bibliographies; the original proof and correction were not read. The later preprint \citet[Introduction, p.~2]{marcoux2026generators}, first posted 21 August 2026, explicitly still calls the exact Hilbert-space problem unsolved.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, no generally accepted solution was verified in the literature checked. The unrestricted Hilbert-space problem remains distinct from its solved special classes and unverified claims.
worth: Worth investigating in precise special classes; the unrestricted problem exceeds a bounded development.

title: Schur positivity of generalized determinants
notes: Generalized determinants of a positive matrix are positive, by Schur.
statement: For Hermitian positive semidefinite \(A=(a_{ij})\) and an irreducible character \(\chi\) of \(S_n\), the immanant \(\sum_{\sigma}\chi(\sigma)\prod_i a_{i,\sigma(i)}\) is nonnegative; it is positive for positive definite \(A\).
reconstruction: Hermitian positivity, irreducible characters and nonnegative in the semidefinite case are supplied.
fate: The antecedent is \citet[pp.~184--207]{schur1918formen}, published June 1918. The particular generalized determinant is not defined in the note.
present_status: As of November 2026, the character-immanant reading is established; entrywise positivity alone is insufficient.

title: WKB transport before a caustic
notes: The wave has an action phase and square-root Jacobian amplitude.
statement:
For \(ih\psi_t=(-h^2\Delta/2+V)\psi\), \(\psi=ae^{iS/h}\) gives \(S_t+|
abla S|^2/2+V=0\) and \(a_t+
abla S\cdot
abla a+(\Delta S)a/2=0\) at leading orders. The amplitude is a transported half-density.
reconstruction: A consistent normalization and formal leading-order interpretation are supplied.
fate: The local equations follow by direct substitution of the ansatz. The Introduction of \citet{arnold1967characteristic} supplies the later Maslov-asymptotic context, not a proof of these transport formulas.
present_status: As of November 2026, the formula applies where the characteristic projection is nonsingular.

title: Characteristic class of caustic phase
notes: Caustic crossings carry a topological phase correction.
statement: A smooth Lagrangian Gauss map pulls back the integral degree-one Maslov class of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. In a standard convention its loop phase is \(\exp(-i\pi\mu/2)\).
reconstruction: The Grassmannian construction is the later precise identification.
fate: \citet[Sections~1--3]{arnold1967characteristic}, received 28 September 1966 and published 1967, gives the characteristic class. These notes witness November 1964 oral circulation.
present_status: As of November 2026, the Maslov-class formulation is established, with convention-dependent phase sign.

title: Experiments and sufficient statistics
notes: Distribution families and statistics are introduced, with a Gaussian sample-mean example.
statement: In a dominated experiment \(\{P_\theta\}\), sufficiency means that the conditional law of the sample given a statistic is independent of \(\theta\). For independent \(N(\theta,\sigma^2)\) observations with known positive variance, the sample mean is sufficient.
reconstruction: Domination, independence and known variance are supplied.
fate: These are classical preliminaries used in \citet[p.~520]{linnik1965cotest}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the Gaussian example needs known variance; the mean alone is insufficient when variance is also unknown.

title: Randomized and similar tests
notes: The source defines randomized tests, then explicitly says \ru{Тесты подобные}: the null rejection probability is \(\alpha\) at every null parameter. A separate later line abbreviates invariant tests.
statement: A randomized test is measurable \(\phi:\Omega\to[0,1]\). Level \(\alpha\) requires \(\sup_{\Theta_0}E_\theta\phi\leq\alpha\); similarity requires equality for every null parameter. Group invariance is a different condition.
reconstruction: The terminology is corrected, not an invariance theorem asserted.
fate: \citet[p.~520]{linnik1965cotest} uses the same similarity definition. The P000039 scan and both supplied transcriptions already distinguish the definition from the later abbreviated invariance remark.
present_status: As of November 2026, level, similarity and group invariance must be distinguished.

title: Normal means with unknown unequal variances
notes: Comparison of two Gaussian means is the nuisance-parameter example.
statement: Given independent samples \(X_i\sim N(\mu_1,\sigma_1^2)\), \(Y_j\sim N(\mu_2,\sigma_2^2)\), with unknown positive variances, test \(\mu_1=\mu_2\). Optimality additionally requires a level, sidedness, admissible test class and alternative power criterion.
reconstruction: The model is normalized; no universal optimum is inferred.
fate: This is the classical Behrens--Fisher setting. \citet[pp.~520--522]{linnik1965cotest} supplies a general weighted optimization framework, not an unrestricted uniformly most powerful solution.
present_status: As of November 2026, the model is definite, but no single remaining optimality conjecture is specified.

title: Bayes-weighted cotest optimization
notes: An alternative measure and a cotest ideal encode the testing constraints.
statement: For a similar test set \(l=\phi-\alpha\). Then \(E_\theta l=0\) on \(\Theta_0\), \(-\alpha\leq l\leq1-\alpha\). A fixed alternative measure \(B\) gives objective \(\int E_\theta l\,dB(\theta)\). Under analytic-transform hypotheses, null-zero constraints become ideal membership.
reconstruction: The bounds and fixed alternative weighting make the problem precise.
fate: \citet[pp.~520--522]{linnik1965cotest} gives this construction. Received 7 December 1964, published 1965, following the seminar by three weeks.
present_status: As of November 2026, the framework is identifiable; its conclusions depend on the transform range and weighting.

title: Analytic ideals in statistical testing
notes: Cartan, Oka and division organize cotest constraints.
statement: A coherent null-constraint ideal on a Stein parameter domain admits global patching of local division by Cartan B. This does not give boundary-continuous division or guarantee that every holomorphic function is a statistical transform.
reconstruction: The Stein/coherent formulation explains the method; not all these hypotheses appear in the note.
fate: \citet[p.~521]{linnik1965cotest} applies analytic-ideal generation under specified conditions on the null set; the application is new, the sheaf machinery older.
present_status: As of November 2026, the analytic reduction is established with those hypotheses.

title: Unspecified primary ideals on a ball
notes: Primary ideals for functions on a ball are mentioned.
statement: No unique mathematical statement can be extracted: the algebra could be holomorphic, bounded holomorphic or boundary-continuous, and no support or ideal is specified.
fate: Linnik/Palamodov/analytic-division searches identify the surrounding programme, but no unique problem; Gorin next states a precise maximal-ideal question.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fragment remains unidentifiable from the supplied evidence; this does not establish that a mathematical problem is open.

title: Coordinate generators of the ball-algebra ideal
notes: If \(f(0)=0\), can \(f=z_1g_1+z_2g_2\), with all functions holomorphic in the ball and continuous on its closure?
statement: For \(A(B^n)=\mathcal O(B^n)\cap C(\overline B^n)\) and \(a\in B^n\), the ideal \(\{f:f(a)=0\}\) is generated by \(z_j-a_j\). The source asks \(n=2,a=0\).
reconstruction: The general \(n,a\) version records the known extension.
fate: \citet[pp.~595--596, reference Hen]{backlundfallstrom1998gleason} records Leibenzon’s affirmative solution and Henkin’s 1971 publication. \citet[pp.~125--132]{gleason1964ideals} is the contemporary antecedent. Initial circulation of Leibenzon’s proof was not verified.
present_status: As of November 2026, the exact ball question is solved; later counterexamples concern other domains.

title: Disk and polydisc division
notes: The one-variable case is immediate and the product domain is easier.
statement: For \(f\in A(\mathbb D)\), \(f(0)=0\), division by \(z\) has a removable singularity and remains boundary-continuous. On \(\mathbb D^n\), successive coordinate telescoping and division produce \(f=\sum z_jg_j\) for \(f(0)=0\).
reconstruction: The telescoping proof is supplied, not a boundary power-series argument.
fate: The one-variable assertion is also recalled by \citet[p.~596]{backlundfallstrom1998gleason}; the telescoping explanation is elementary reconstruction.
present_status: As of November 2026, the division holds without assuming uniform boundary convergence of Taylor series.

title: Division without boundary restrictions
notes: The difficulty disappears when boundary continuity is dropped.
statement: For Stein \(\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n\) and \(a\in\Omega\), the coherent ideal sheaf of \(a\) is generated by \(z_j-a_j\). Cartan B applied to its relation sheaf yields \(f=\sum(z_j-a_j)g_j\), \(g_j\in\mathcal O(\Omega)\), when \(f(a)=0\).
reconstruction: The sheaf proof and Stein hypothesis are editorial.
fate: The holomorphic-versus-Banach-algebra distinction is explicit in \citet[pp.~595--596]{backlundfallstrom1998gleason}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the holomorphic statement gives no boundary continuity estimate.

title: Hamilton--Jacobi equation
notes: An exponential substitution relates Schrödinger evolution to classical trajectories.
statement: For \(ih\psi_t=(-h^2\Delta/2+V)\psi\), \(\psi=e^{iS/h}(a_0+ha_1+\cdots)\) yields \(S_t+H(x,\nabla S)=0\), \(H=|p|^2/2+V\), formally wherever \(S\) is smooth.
reconstruction: Signs, kinetic factor and the formal interpretation are normalized.
fate: This local background is used in \citet[Introduction]{arnold1967characteristic}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the formal relation is standard; the notebook coefficients cannot all hold simultaneously.

title: Action and half-density
notes: The amplitude contains a square-root trajectory Jacobian and the phase \(\int p\,dx\).
statement: For nonsingular \(x=X_t(y)\), \(a_0(t,X_t(y))=a_0(0,y)|\det D_yX_t|^{-1/2}\). The action evolves by \(S(t,X_t(y))=S(0,y)+\int_0^t(p\cdot\dot x-H)\,ds\).
reconstruction: Absolute Jacobian and \(-Hdt\) are supplied.
fate: The geometric setting is \citet[Introduction]{arnold1967characteristic}; these consistent formulas are an editorial reconstruction.
present_status: As of November 2026, the formula requires a nonsingular projection; abbreviated spatial action needs a fixed-energy or time convention.

title: Maslov correction at caustics
notes: A branch sum is corrected by a phase involving \(\pi n_j/2\), associated with Maslov.
statement: For regular Lagrangian propagation, oscillatory-integral chart transitions yield Maslov phase factors; the integral Maslov class governs loop phase, conventionally \(e^{-i\pi\mu/2}\).
reconstruction: The phase sign is conventional; the damaged formula does not determine it.
fate: \citet[Sections~1--3]{arnold1967characteristic} gives the topological formulation, received September 1966 and published 1967, after these lectures.
present_status: As of November 2026, the phase class is established; uniform local approximation needs a caustic normal form.

title: Optical quarter-cycle phase
notes: A ray tangent to an envelope acquires a phase jump \(\pi/2\).
statement: At a generic fold caustic, an Airy model matches oscillatory branches with a relative quarter-cycle phase under standard conventions. Degenerate caustics require different models.
reconstruction: Genericity and phase convention supplied.
fate: This optical motivation precedes the seminar and informs \citet[Introduction]{arnold1967characteristic}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fold qualification is necessary.

title: Morse index and conjugate points
notes: The phase index is related to negative squares of the second variation and conjugate points.
statement: For a regular fixed-endpoint mechanical extremal with positive kinetic form and nonconjugate endpoints, the Morse index equals the count of interior conjugate points with multiplicities.
reconstruction: Regularity, endpoints and multiplicity conventions supplied.
fate: The classical variational theorem is background to \citet[Sections~1--3]{arnold1967characteristic}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the relation holds in that variational setting; endpoint nullity requires an extra convention.

title: Phase-volume eigenvalue asymptotics
notes: Berezin relates a region under the classical Hamiltonian to quantum eigenvalue counting; the written threshold mixes energy and index.
statement: Let \(d\ge1\), \(V\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R)\), and \(V(x)\to+\infty\) as \(|x|\to\infty\). Let \(P_h=-h^2\Delta/2+V\) be its self-adjoint Schr\"odinger realization on \(L^2(\mathbb R^d)\), and let \(N_h(E)\) count eigenvalues below \(E\), with multiplicity. For \(E>\min V\) a regular value of \(|p|^2/2+V(x)\), \[ N_h(E)\sim(2\pi h)^{-d} \operatorname{vol}\{(x,p):|p|^2/2+V(x)<E\}\quad(h\downarrow0). \] The phase volume is finite and positive.
reconstruction: Limit, normalization, dimension and confinement are supplied.
fate: The historical eigenvalue-counting antecedent is \citet[pp.~110--117]{weyl1911eigenvalues}. The stated semiclassical Schrödinger version is a modern reconstruction; neither the 1911 paper’s original Laplace problem nor the notebook’s compressed wording is identical to this full formulation.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed Weyl law is established under those hypotheses.
speaker: F. A. Berezin

title: Sturm zeros and interlacing
notes: Dirichlet eigenfunctions on \([0,\pi]\) are discussed; the free eigenvalues have a negative sign in the note.
statement: For real continuous \(q\), the Dirichlet operator \(L=-d^2/dx^2+q\) has simple ordered eigenvalues. Its \(j\)-th eigenfunction has \(j-1\) interior zeros interlacing the next. For \(q=0\), \(\lambda_j=j^2\).
reconstruction: Indexing starts at 1 throughout.
fate: \citet[historical discussion and Sturm theorem]{berardhelffer2020sturm} revisits the 1836 result; preprint 2017, publication 2020.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is classical; the notebook sign is erroneous for its displayed operator.

title: Zeros of the first eigenfunction span
notes: A linear combination of the first eigenfunctions has a bounded number of zeros; indexing changes within the note.
statement: For a regular real Dirichlet Sturm--Liouville problem with smooth potential, a nonzero combination of the first \(m\) eigenfunctions has at most \(m-1\) interior zeros, counted with multiplicity.
reconstruction: The indexing and interior multiplicity convention resolve the ambiguity.
fate: \citet[main theorem and historical discussion]{berardhelffer2020sturm} identifies Sturm’s 1836 theorem; the preprint circulated June 2017 before 2020 publication.
present_status: As of November 2026, the bound is established; the seminar’s distinctive feature is its proof strategy.

title: Gelfand’s Slater-determinant proof strategy
notes: A determinant of eigenfunction data is related to a many-particle problem; the displayed entries mix values and derivatives.
statement: \(\det[u_j(x_i)]_{i,j=1}^m\) is an antisymmetric eigenfunction of \(\sum_i L_{x_i}\). On \(x_1<\cdots<x_m\), it is a ground state of fixed sign, so the evaluation determinant is nonzero for distinct interior points. Multiplicity of zeros requires an additional argument.
reconstruction: Ordered chamber, ground-state argument and the multiplicity distinction are supplied.
fate: \citet[Sections~3--6]{berardhelffer2020gelfand} explicitly implements Gelfand’s strategy: first preprint 11 July 2018, journal 2020.
present_status: As of November 2026, the strategy has a rigorous published realization; the notebook determinant alone is incomplete.

title: Congruence property for integer special linear groups
notes: For \(n\geq3\), every finite-index subgroup of \(SL(n,\mathbb Z)\) contains a congruence subgroup; \(n=2\) differs.
statement: For \(n\geq3\) and finite-index \(\Gamma\leq SL_n(\mathbb Z)\), some \(m\geq1\) satisfies \(\ker(SL_n(\mathbb Z)\to SL_n(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z))\subset\Gamma\). For \(n=2\), finite-index noncongruence subgroups exist.
reconstruction: The subgroup need not be normal; passage to its finite-index core is allowed.
fate: \citet[Sections~1.2--1.3, Theorem~1 and historical remark]{serre1968congruence} attributes the rational-integer case to Bass--Lazard--Serre and Mennicke in 1964; the Bourbaki lecture was June 1967, printed 1968.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated integer-matrix theorem is settled, not a February 1965 open question.

title: Reduction to powers of elementary transvections
notes: The normal subgroup generated by powers of elementary matrices is used to reduce the finite-index question.
statement: Given a finite-index subgroup, its normal core contains \(e_{ij}(m)\) for some common positive \(m\), since each elementary generator has finite-order image in the finite quotient. For \(n\geq3\), the congruence theorem then controls the normal elementary subgroup.
reconstruction: Normal core and common multiple of finite orders are supplied.
fate: This is the elementary-matrix route in the congruence programme summarized by \citet[Sections~2--3]{serre1968congruence}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the finite-quotient reduction is valid; identifying elementary and principal congruence subgroups at the same level is not automatic.

title: Rank-one power quotients and triangle groups
notes: For \(n=2\), powers of generators are said to give infinite index, with a quotient interpreted as a surface fundamental group.
statement: In \(PSL_2(\mathbb Z)=\langle s,t:s^2=(st)^3=1\rangle\), adding \(t^m=1\) gives the triangle group \(\Delta(2,3,m)\). For \(2\leq m\leq5\) it is finite, for \(m=6\) Euclidean, and for \(m\geq7\) hyperbolic. It is an orbifold group, not generally a torsion-free surface group.
reconstruction: Passage from SL to PSL and the triangle-group presentation are essential.
fate: The modular-group contrast is classical; \citet[Section~1.2(b)]{serre1968congruence} confirms the failure of the rank-one congruence property. The explicit presentation and low-level check here are editorial algebra.
present_status: As of November 2026, the unqualified infinite-index and surface-group assertions are false; a torsion-free finite-index subgroup restores the surface interpretation in the hyperbolic case.

title: Unspecified elementary congruence transformation
notes: An \(a\equiv b\pmod N\) statement is linked to elementary transformations.
statement: No unique mathematical statement can be extracted: the entries, matrix operation, modulus conventions and desired normal form are not defined.
fate: Congruence-subgroup sources explain the surrounding method but do not identify this isolated transformation.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fragment remains unidentifiable from the supplied evidence; this does not establish that a mathematical problem is open.

title: SU(6) spin-flavour symmetry
notes: Spin SU(2) and internal SU(3) are combined in SU(6).
statement: The tensor product on \(\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^3\) embeds \(SU(2)\times SU(3)\) into \(SU(6)\). This organizes a nonrelativistic approximate spin-flavour model; it is not by itself a Lorentz-covariant exact scattering symmetry.
reconstruction: The approximation status and tensor-product interpretation are supplied.
fate: \citet[pp.~173--175]{gurseyradicati1964spin} appeared 3 August 1964; \citet[pp.~B1756--B1760]{sakita1964supermultiplets} was received 7 August and published 21 December 1964. Both precede this February record.
present_status: As of November 2026, the historical SU(6) construction is identified; exact relativistic symmetry needs additional assumptions.

title: Hermitian matrices and the Poincaré group
notes: Lorentz transformations act on Hermitian matrices; a block matrix with diagonal \(A,(A^*)^{-1}\) and Hermitian upper-right block is written.
statement: For \(A\in SL_2(\mathbb C)\), \(X=X^*\), the map \(X\mapsto AXA^*\) preserves \(\det X=x_0^2-|\mathbf x|^2\). The covering Poincaré group has law \((A,X)(B,Y)=(AB,X+AYA^*)\), represented by \(\begin{pmatrix}A&X(A^*)^{-1}\\0&(A^*)^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\).
reconstruction: The semidirect product and corrected block are editorial. Setting translations to zero gives the Lorentz cover; spatial rotations require \(A\in SU(2)\).
fate: This is the standard spacetime group underlying \citet[p.~1251]{colemanmandula1967symmetries}; the block-law repair is direct matrix algebra.
present_status: As of November 2026, the corrected matrices are closed under multiplication. An arbitrary Hermitian upper-right block in the notebook parametrization is not closed.

title: Combining spacetime and internal symmetries
notes: A larger symmetry containing relativistic and internal transformations is sought.
statement: For a nontrivial analytic scattering matrix in four-dimensional relativistic theory, suppose a connected ordinary Lie symmetry contains the Poincaré group, acts tensorially on multiparticle states, has only finitely many particle types below each mass bound, and satisfies the regularity and nontrivial-scattering hypotheses of Coleman--Mandula. Then it is locally a direct product of Poincaré and internal symmetries.
reconstruction: The precise scattering question is a later formulation; no blanket impossibility theorem is attributed to the notebook.
fate: \citet[p.~1251, theorem and hypotheses~1--5]{colemanmandula1967symmetries}, received March and published July 1967, gives this restricted obstruction. The original broad programme is not equivalent to the theorem’s hypotheses.
present_status: As of November 2026, the ordinary-Lie scattering version is settled; graded symmetries and violations of the hypotheses lie outside that conclusion.

title: 108- and 144-parameter proposals
notes: Groups with 108 and 144 parameters are proposed in the discussion.
statement: No unique mathematical statement can be extracted: no Lie brackets, real form, faithful action or particle interpretation identifies the groups uniquely.
fate: SU(6), relativistic supermultiplet and Coleman--Mandula searches contextualize the numbers but do not establish a unique match.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fragment remains unidentifiable from the supplied evidence; this does not establish that a mathematical problem is open.

title: Primary ideals through differential conditions
notes: A primary ideal and its prime radical are compared, with a square inclusion and derivations vanishing on the smaller ideal; I and J are later explicitly interchanged.
statement: Let \(A=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), \(\operatorname{char}k=0\), \(P\) prime and \(Q\) \(P\)-primary with \(P^2\subset Q\subset P\). Over \(K=\operatorname{Frac}(A/P)\), linear functionals on \(P A_P/P^2A_P\) annihilating \(QA_P/P^2A_P\), extended as first-order operators, detect membership in \(Q\) together with evaluation modulo \(P\). General primary ideals require higher-order operators.
reconstruction: Prime/primary letters, generic localization, polynomial ring, characteristic zero and operator values are supplied.
fate: The established Noetherian-operator theory is made algebraically and algorithmically explicit by \citet[Theorem~2.1 and Sections~4--6]{cidruizhomssturmfels2021primary}, preprint January 2020, journal 2021. Its introduction traces Palamodov’s correction of constant-coefficient claims.
present_status: As of November 2026, the method is established; constant-coefficient operators do not suffice for every primary ideal.

title: Conormal module and derivations
notes: Derivations are used as linear functionals on an ideal modulo its square.
statement: For a \(k\)-algebra \(A\), ideal \(J\), and \(A/J\)-module \(M\), any \(k\)-derivation \(D:A\to M\) kills \(J^2\) and restricts to an \(A/J\)-linear map \(J/J^2\to M\). Extension of every such functional requires additional smoothness or splitting assumptions.
reconstruction: The module structure and the direction of the assertion are made explicit.
fate: This is standard conormal/differential algebra, used in the modern algebraic framework of \citet[Section~5]{cidruizhomssturmfels2021primary}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the restriction statement is valid; surjectivity of the extension map is not automatic for an arbitrary quotient.

title: Lifting across a square-zero ideal
notes: A quotient-field embedding is lifted; a square-root equation is corrected by an element of the ideal.
statement: If \(J^2=0\) in a commutative ring and \(x_0^2-y\in J\), with \(2x_0\) a unit, then \(x=x_0-(2x_0)^{-1}(x_0^2-y)\) satisfies \(x^2=y\). Lifting an entire residue field uses separability/formal smoothness, not merely that the quotient is a field.
reconstruction: Square-zero, invertibility and separability conditions are reconstructed.
fate: The displayed square-zero correction is elementary Hensel-style algebra; the general coefficient-field statement needs the extra hypotheses made explicit here.
present_status: As of November 2026, the corrected lifting formula holds; a completely arbitrary quotient need not split.

title: Polynomial derivations, localization and formal flow
notes: Operators are written as sums \(P_i\partial_i\), extended to fractions and associated with a formal motion.
statement: A \(k\)-derivation of \(k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) is \(\sum D(x_i)\partial_i\); it extends uniquely to a localization by \(D(a/s)=(sD(a)-aD(s))/s^2\). In characteristic zero, \(\exp(tD)\) is an algebra map to \(A[[t]]\); analytic convergence is a separate issue.
reconstruction: Derivation rather than arbitrary differential operator, and formal rather than convergent flow, are supplied.
fate: This is classical differential algebra; the distinction between derivations and higher-order differential operators is explicit in \citet[Section~5]{cidruizhomssturmfels2021primary}.
present_status: As of November 2026, these formal identities hold; the notebook formula does not describe every differential operator.

title: The solution should be an ideal
notes: The discussion concludes that a solution should form an ideal.
statement: No unique mathematical statement can be extracted: the space of solutions, ring action and equations are not specified. Kernels of arbitrary differential operators are not ideals.
fate: Primary-ideal/Noetherian-operator sources clarify a possible intended compatibility condition but do not identify this isolated sentence.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fragment remains unidentifiable from the supplied evidence; this does not establish that a mathematical problem is open.

title: Primary-ideal quotient by compatible differential jets
notes: For a polynomial primary ideal \(J\), the quotient \(\mathcal H/J\mathcal H\) is represented by restrictions \(d(z,D)F|_N\), with local realizability.
statement: For a coherent ideal \(\mathcal J\) on a Stein domain \(\Omega\), a faithful differential-jet realization of \(\mathcal O_\Omega/\mathcal J\), when chosen, has kernel \(\mathcal J\); compatible locally realizable data globalize by Cartan B. For polynomial primary ideals, suitable Noetherian operators provide such finite-order descriptions with the necessary localization and compatibility conditions.
reconstruction: Steinness, coherent quotient, operator choice and local compatibility are supplied; the 1961 smooth theorem is deliberately kept separate.
fate: \citet[Part~I]{palamodov1970operators} is the speaker’s subsequent systematic treatment (English 1970). \citet[Theorems~1--2]{palamodov1961ideals} is a prior smooth-function analogue, not the identical holomorphic theorem. The exact section and first publication of this formulation were not verified.
present_status: As of November 2026, the Noetherian-operator and coherent-quotient framework is established, but arbitrary unrestricted vector data on \(N\) are not the target.

title: Unspecified growth-controlled division estimate
notes: An inequality involving the size or growth of the representing function is mentioned after the quotient theorem.
statement: No unique mathematical statement can be extracted: the norm, growth weight, domain geometry and constants are absent.
fate: Palamodov’s 1966 An analytic problem arising in statistics (Doklady 168, 1251--1253; MathNet dan32367 opened) proves a weighted holomorphic division theorem on polydiscs. This is a related outcome, not a verified match to the missing estimate. A later nearby result is \citet[p.~1251, Theorem~1]{palamodov1966statistics}, received 2 August 1965 and published 1966: it treats holomorphic functions of polynomial boundary growth on a polydisc and polynomial-matrix multiplication. Its explicit topology does not identify the unspecified space in the note.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fragment remains unidentifiable from the supplied evidence; this does not establish that a mathematical problem is open.

title: Local linear maps are differential operators
notes: A morphism of sheaves of smooth bundle sections is said to be differential.
statement: A linear morphism of sheaves of smooth sections of finite-rank bundles on a smooth manifold is locally a finite-order differential operator (Peetre’s theorem). The order need not be globally bounded on a noncompact base.
reconstruction: Linearity, finite-rank smooth bundles and local order are explicit.
fate: \citet[pp.~211--218]{peetre1959differential}, with \citet[pp.~116--120]{peetre1960correction}, predates the seminar.
present_status: As of November 2026, the local finite-order assertion is established; linearity and the sheaf locality condition are necessary.

title: Principal symbol and overdetermined ellipticity
notes: The principal matrix symbol is placed over a tangent bundle and called elliptic when a monomorphism.
statement: For an order-\(m\) operator \(A:C^\infty(E)\to C^\infty(F)\), \(\sigma_m(A)(x,\xi):E_x\to F_x\) is homogeneous in \(\xi\in T_x^*X\). Injectivity for real \(\xi\ne0\) is overdetermined ellipticity; an isomorphism is determined ellipticity.
reconstruction: Cotangent bundle and real nonzero covectors supplied.
fate: \citet[p.~423]{atiyahsinger1963index} explicitly places the symbol over the cotangent sphere and defines the isomorphism case.
present_status: As of November 2026, the modern distinction is standard; tangent and cotangent require a chosen metric to identify.

title: Finiteness of every solution-sheaf cohomology group
notes: For \(\ker A\) on a compact manifold, all cohomology groups are stated to be finite-dimensional.
statement: No unique mathematical statement can be extracted: the stated injective-symbol condition alone does not specify the exact compatibility resolution used in the proof. A sufficient precise theorem assumes a finite elliptic differential complex resolving the solution sheaf; then compactness yields finite-dimensional cohomology.
fate: Elliptic-complex and Cartan finiteness sources identify the intended method but not a theorem in the full unstated generality of this sentence.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fragment remains unidentifiable from the supplied evidence; this does not establish that a mathematical problem is open.

title: Two-term fine resolution in the locally solvable case
notes: \(0\to\ker A\to\mathcal E(E_0)\to\mathcal E(E_1)\) is treated as a fine resolution.
statement: If \(A\) is locally surjective as a map of smooth-section sheaves, then \(0\to\ker A\to\mathcal E(E_0)\xrightarrow A\mathcal E(E_1)\to0\) is exact. Therefore \(H^0=\ker A(X)\), \(H^1=\operatorname{coker}A(X)\), and \(H^q=0\) for \(q\ge2\). For a determined elliptic operator on compact boundaryless \(X\), the two displayed global spaces are finite-dimensional.
reconstruction: The terminal zero, local surjectivity and no-boundary condition are supplied.
fate: The resolution principle is \citet[Section~1, Proposition~1]{cartan1954finitude}; elliptic kernel/cokernel finiteness appears in \citet[p.~423]{atiyahsinger1963index}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the conclusion is valid with local exactness; omitting it makes the resolution argument incomplete.

title: De Rham and coherent-sheaf finiteness
notes: De Rham forms, holomorphic functions, Kodaira and Cartan are examples of the sheaf approach.
statement: The de Rham complex is a fine resolution of the constant real sheaf. On a compact complex manifold every coherent analytic sheaf has finite-dimensional cohomology. These are separate statements; the holomorphic structure sheaf is not fine.
reconstruction: Coherence and the distinct resolutions are explicit.
fate: \citet[p.~17-1 and Section~1]{cartan1954finitude}, lecture 3 May 1954, states coherent finiteness and the de Rham example; its reference~1 is Cartan--Serre’s 1953 announcement.
present_status: As of November 2026, both examples are classical; they require their respective smooth or analytic hypotheses.

title: Compact comparison on resolutions
notes: Banach/Fréchet sheaves, different resolutions and a compact comparison inducing identity on cohomology are proposed.
statement: If two resolutions have continuous chain maps inducing inverse maps on cohomology, and the composite induces a compact identity on a Hausdorff Banach cohomology space, that space is finite-dimensional. Closed ranges and quotient topologies are necessary in this formulation.
reconstruction: Hausdorff Banach cohomology, continuity and closed-range requirements are supplied.
fate: The analytic finiteness method is exemplified by \citet[proof of the finiteness theorem]{cartan1954finitude}; the source invokes a Schwartz compactness lemma without its precise functional-analytic hypotheses.
present_status: As of November 2026, the compact-identity argument works in the reconstructed setting; an arbitrary non-Hausdorff quotient does not qualify.

title: Identity plus compact operator at a point
notes: For a one-point space the sheaf question becomes identity plus a compact operator.
statement: For a Banach space \(X\) and compact linear \(K:X\to X\), \(I+K\) is Fredholm with index zero.
reconstruction: Banach topology and linear compactness supplied.
fate: This is classical Riesz--Fredholm theory, contained in the framework for perturbations by compact operators recalled by \citet[p.~861]{smale1965sard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the point case is established, including closed range and finite-dimensional kernel/cokernel.
