title: Elementary sphere obstructions and examples
notes: Even spheres have no nonzero field; odd spheres have one; \(S^3,S^7\) are parallelizable.
statement: For even \(n>0\), \(\chi(S^n)=2\) obstructs a nowhere-zero tangent field. On \(S^{2m-1}\subset\mathbb C^m\), \(x\mapsto ix\) is tangent and nonzero. Quaternionic and octonionic multiplication give frames on \(S^3,S^7\).
reconstruction: The explicit complex multiplication and \(n>0\) convention are supplied.
fate: These classical examples precede the upper-bound theorem of \citet[Section~1]{adams1962vector}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the assertions hold; \(S^1\) is also parallelizable.

title: Block extension of tangent fields
notes: An existing field is applied separately to coordinate blocks, multiplied by their norms.
statement: From continuous independent tangent fields \(v_1,\ldots,v_k\) on \(S^{m-1}\), define on \(S^{pm-1}\) the block field \(w_i(y_1,\ldots,y_p)=(|y_j|v_i(y_j/|y_j|))_j\), with zero at a zero block. These are continuous, tangent and independent; smooth approximation preserves independence.
reconstruction: Zero-block convention and the continuity/smoothing distinction are supplied.
fate: This elementary construction supplies lower-bound intuition in the setting of \citet[Section~1]{adams1962vector}. Its formula is directly checkable from the notebook.
present_status: As of November 2026, the extension works; differentiability at a zero block is not automatic for the raw formula.

title: Hurwitz--Radon--Adams number
notes: Write \(m=2^b(2a+1)\), \(b=c+4d\), \(0\leq c\leq3\); the maximum number is \(2^c+8d-1\).
statement: If \(m=(2a+1)2^{4d+c}\), then \(S^{m-1}\) has exactly \(\rho(m)-1\) independent continuous tangent fields, where \(\rho(m)=8d+2^c\).
reconstruction: The main boxed formula is correct; a later prose periodicity sentence is corrected separately.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.1]{adams1962vector}, received November 1961 and published 1962, proves the matching upper bound to the classical lower construction.
present_status: As of November 2026, the number is exact in every dimension. Multiplication of \(m\) by 16, not 6, increases it by 8.

title: Stable vector bundles and KO
notes: Stable equivalence, direct sums, tensor products and the real K-functor are described.
statement: For compact \(X\), \(KO^0(X)\) is the Grothendieck group of real vector bundles, with tensor-product multiplication. For connected based \(X\), \(\widetilde{KO}^0(X)\) is the rank-zero subgroup. Stable equivalence of actual bundles alone forgets rank and must be distinguished from full \(KO^0\).
reconstruction: Group completion and reduced group are distinguished.
fate: This is the K-theoretic language of \citet[Sections~1--2]{adams1962vector}; the index-theory use appears already in \citet[p.~423]{atiyahsinger1963index} for complex K-theory.
present_status: As of November 2026, the unreduced/reduced distinction resolves the notebook’s missing rank summand.

title: Bott periodicity and stable groups
notes: The stable orthogonal groups recur with period eight and nontrivial entries at residues 0,1,2,4.
statement: \(KO^{-j}(\mathrm{pt})\), for \(j=0,\ldots,7\), is respectively \(\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2,\mathbb Z/2,0,\mathbb Z,0,0,0\), repeating with period eight. For \(i>0\), \(\widetilde{KO}^0(S^i)=\pi_i(BO)\).
reconstruction: The table is in KO-degree conventions, not unshifted \(\pi_i(O)\).
fate: \citet[Introduction, stable classical-group periodicity]{bott1959stable}, received November 1958 and published September 1959, is the primary source.
present_status: As of November 2026, periodicity is established; the sphere formula requires reduced K-theory.

title: Real K-theory of projective space
notes: The reduced group is cyclic; the tautological class satisfies \(v^2=1\), \(\lambda=v-1\), \(\lambda^2=-2\lambda\). The order is once described as \(f(k)\).
statement: For \(k\ge1\), let \(\phi(k)\) count \(1\le j\le k\) congruent to \(0,1,2,4\pmod8\). Then \(KO^0(\mathbb{RP}^k)=\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2^{\phi(k)}\), with reduced generator \(\lambda=[\gamma]-1\), satisfying \(\lambda^2=-2\lambda\).
reconstruction: The tautological bundle is reduced by subtracting the trivial line; the exponent is defined explicitly.
fate: The real-projective computation is part of \citet[projective-space K-theory calculation]{adams1962vector}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the correct order is \(2^{\phi(k)}\), in agreement with another line of the same notebook.

title: Reflection map and stunted projective space
notes: An axis determines an orthogonal reflection; a stunted projective quotient maps into a Stiefel quotient.
statement: For integers \(n\ge2\) and \(0\le k\le n-2\), the map \([v]\mapsto I-2vv^t\) from \(\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}\) to \(O(n)\), for unit \(v\), induces \(\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}/\mathbb{RP}^{n-k-2}\to O(n)/O(n-k-1)\) by taking the last \(k+1\) columns. The collapsed subspace is precisely where those coordinates of \(v\) vanish.
reconstruction: A specific block convention for the Stiefel quotient is supplied.
fate: Stunted projective spaces are central to \citet[Theorem~1.2 and ensuing reduction]{adams1962vector}. The explicit reflection formula is editorial clarification of the drawing.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is well-defined; indexing must match the chosen Stiefel frame size.

title: Noetherian differential jets and the algebraic proof
notes: \(\mathcal H/J\mathcal H\cong\mathcal H\{J\}\), with \(\mathcal H\{J\}\) locally realized by \(d(z,D)F|_N\); Kazhdan is said to obtain this algebraically.
statement: The quotient is represented by compatible finite differential jets on the primary support, once suitable Noetherian operators and the locally realizable target sheaf are fixed. Algebraically, a primary ideal in characteristic-zero polynomial rings is the simultaneous vanishing modulo its radical of finitely many polynomial-coefficient differential operators.
reconstruction: The operator construction and target compatibility are supplied; no attribution of the modern algorithm to Kazhdan is made.
fate: The speaker’s systematic treatment is \citet[Part~I]{palamodov1970operators}; the algebraic operator statement is explicitly formulated in \citet[Theorem~2.1 and equation~(17)]{cidruizhomssturmfels2021primary}. The latter circulated January 2020, published 2021.
present_status: As of November 2026, the framework is established; the note does not identify a separate Kazhdan publication or supply all analytic globalization hypotheses.

title: Essential self-adjointness and boundary conditions
notes: The range of \(A-\lambda\) is required to be dense for every complex \(\lambda\); differentiation on an interval is compared with periodic boundary conditions.
statement: For a densely defined symmetric \(A\), essential self-adjointness is equivalent to density of both \(\operatorname{ran}(A-i)\) and \(\operatorname{ran}(A+i)\). On \(L^2(0,1)\), \(i\,d/dx\) on \(H^1_0(0,1)\) has deficiency indices \((1,1)\); the periodic \(H^1\) domain gives a self-adjoint extension.
reconstruction: Dense domain, the nonreal parameters, and the precise Sobolev domains are supplied.
fate: These are the operator-theoretic preliminaries to \citet[Sections~9--10]{nelson1959analytic}. The range criterion needs a pair of nonreal parameters, not all complex numbers.
present_status: As of November 2026, the distinction between a symmetric operator, its closure and a chosen self-adjoint extension is essential.

title: Commuting on a domain does not imply strong commutation
notes: \(A,B\) commute on an invariant dense domain, and all real linear combinations are essentially self-adjoint, yet their exponentials need not commute.
statement: There exist symmetric \(A,B\) on a common invariant dense domain \(D\), with \(ABf=BAf\) for \(f\in D\), such that every \(aA+bB\), \(a,b\in\mathbb R\), is essentially self-adjoint on \(D\), while the spectral measures of their closures do not commute.
reconstruction: The distinction between algebraic commutation and commuting spectral measures is explicit.
fate: \citet[Section~10]{nelson1959analytic}, published 1959, constructs precisely this obstruction. Essential self-adjointness of a sum of squares is a stronger sufficient integrability condition.
present_status: As of November 2026, the counterexample remains valid; separate essential self-adjointness does not license joint functional calculus.

title: The punctured genus-four translation surface
notes: A planar region with an inner square removed is glued by translations; after identification of corner points, it is a genus-four surface minus one point.
statement: On Nelson’s translation surface, \(X=\partial_x,Y=\partial_y\) commute locally on \(C_c^\infty\). Almost-everywhere complete straight-line flows generate unitary groups on area \(L^2\); \(iX,iY\), and every real linear combination, are essentially self-adjoint on this domain. The two global flows fail to commute across the missing point.
reconstruction: The invariant area measure, compactly supported smooth domain and factors of \(i\) are supplied.
fate: \citet[Section~10; Russian translation pp.~121--123]{nelson1959analytic} explicitly gives genus four. The notebook drawing agrees; replacing four by two would introduce an error.
present_status: As of November 2026, the geometric example is established and the source genus is retained.

title: The Laplacian obstruction to integrating the Lie algebra
notes: If the Laplacian were self-adjoint, all fields would generate the expected group; therefore the example’s Laplacian is not essentially self-adjoint.
statement: For a representation of a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra by skew-symmetric operators \(X_j\) on a common invariant dense domain, essential self-adjointness of the Nelson Laplacian \(-\sum_jX_j^2\) is a sufficient condition for integration to a unitary representation of the simply connected group. Thus this sufficient condition fails for Nelson’s noncommuting translation example.
reconstruction: A common invariant domain, the simply connected integrating group and the sign convention are supplied.
fate: \citet[Section~9, integrability theorem, and Section~10]{nelson1959analytic} proves the criterion and applies it to the example.
present_status: As of November 2026, the conclusion concerns essential self-adjointness on the specified domain; it does not deny the existence of self-adjoint extensions.

title: Spectral construction of the unitary evolution
notes: The exponent of a self-adjoint operator is written using an unnormalized resolvent integral, and the differential equation \(u_t=iAu\) is invoked.
statement: For self-adjoint \(A\), \(e^{itA}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{it\lambda}\,dE_A(\lambda)\). This is a strongly continuous unitary group on all \(H\); strong differentiation solves \(u_t=iAu\) for initial vectors in \(D(A)\). Resolvent boundary values recover \(E_A\) through Stone’s jump formula, not through the unqualified integral in the note.
reconstruction: Spectral measure, normalization and differentiability domain are supplied.
fate: The spectral and unitary-group framework is used throughout \citet[Sections~9--10]{nelson1959analytic}; the displayed correction follows directly from spectral calculus.
present_status: As of November 2026, the unitary evolution is established, with a domain condition for strong differentiability.

title: Simplicity of eigenvalues for an ergodic system
notes: For an ergodic system every eigenvalue is simple; invariant functions are constant.
statement: For an ergodic probability-preserving \(\mathbb Z\)-action or \(\mathbb R\)-flow, each Koopman eigenspace is one-dimensional. A nonzero eigenfunction has constant modulus, and the ratio of two eigenfunctions for the same character is invariant. This does not assert simple continuous spectrum.
reconstruction: Probability preservation and the distinction between eigenspaces and continuous multiplicity are supplied.
fate: The classical pure-point classification is restated precisely in \citet[Introduction and Theorem~5.5]{hermlekreidler2023halmos}; its antecedent is Halmos--von Neumann (1942).
present_status: As of November 2026, the statement is correct under ergodicity; the source heading concerns discrete spectrum.

title: Absolute continuity versus homogeneous Lebesgue spectrum
notes: Correlation functions are Fourier transforms of integrable densities, and a constant spectral multiplicity is called homogeneous.
statement: For the centered Koopman space \(L^2_0(X,\mu)\), absolute continuity means every scalar spectral measure is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on \(\mathbb R\) for flows or Haar measure on \(\mathbb T\) for transformations. Lebesgue maximal type additionally means equivalence of measure classes; homogeneous multiplicity means the multiplicity function is almost everywhere constant.
reconstruction: Centered space, measure-class equivalence and the time-group distinction are explicit.
fate: \citet[Introduction, pp.~899--900]{sinai1961lebesgue} distinguishes the homogeneous Lebesgue conclusion and proves countable multiplicity in its class of flows.
present_status: As of November 2026, absolute continuity alone does not guarantee full Lebesgue maximal type or homogeneous multiplicity; constants must be removed.

title: Historical multiplicity remark and an editorial Banach comparison
notes: All known examples of systems with Lebesgue spectrum are said to have countably infinite multiplicity. There is no explicit existence question, no Banach attribution, and no fixed choice between transformations and flows.
statement: The exact source claim is historical. An editorial comparison asks whether an ergodic probability-preserving transformation or flow can have simple Lebesgue spectrum on \(L^2_0\); these are different questions. The notebook does not uniquely specify either as a proposed problem.
reconstruction: The modern comparison is editorial, the flow/transformation distinction is supplied, and the 2026 claim is separated from verified established results.
fate: For flows, \citet[main result]{prikhodko2020flows} gives a positive construction; the paper was received in June 2012, revised October 2019, and published 2020. For transformations, \citet[Introduction, main theorem]{openai2026lebesgue}, dated 23 September 2026, claims a smooth volume-preserving three-torus diffeomorphism with a bilateral Koopman orbit forming an orthonormal basis of \(L^2_0\). Its theorem statement was inspected, but its proof was not independently verified here.
present_status: As of November 2026, simple Lebesgue flows have a published construction; a new transformation claim exists, and this audit does not establish an accepted resolution of the transformation problem. Neither modern question is assigned to the notebook as an explicit conjecture.

title: Hyperbolic toral automorphisms have countable Lebesgue spectrum
notes: The integer-matrix automorphism of the two-torus is diagonalized by Fourier modes whose integer labels run in infinite orbits.
statement: For \(A\in SL(2,\mathbb Z)\) with \(|\operatorname{tr}A|>2\), the automorphism \(x\mapsto Ax\) of the Haar probability torus has on \(L^2_0\) homogeneous countably infinite Lebesgue spectrum: each orbit of \(A^t\) on \(\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{0\}\) gives a bilateral shift.
reconstruction: Haar probability, removal of constants and hyperbolicity are supplied.
fate: \citet[p.~899]{sinai1961lebesgue} identifies compact abelian-group automorphisms among the already known algebraic examples. The Fourier-orbit argument is explicit in the notebook.
present_status: As of November 2026, the result holds under hyperbolicity; an arbitrary matrix in \(SL(2,\mathbb Z)\) need not satisfy it.

title: Bernoulli shifts have countable Lebesgue spectrum
notes: A tensor product of independent coordinates is organized into translation orbits.
statement: A nontrivial two-sided Bernoulli shift on a standard probability product has homogeneous countably infinite Lebesgue spectrum on \(L^2_0\). Finite tensor words in centered coordinate basis vectors form an orthonormal basis; their shift orbits are free and countably many.
reconstruction: Nontrivial base, two-sided shift, separability and centered space supplied.
fate: This is a classical example within the discrete-time Kolmogorov setting recalled in \citet[Introduction, pp.~899--900]{sinai1961lebesgue}. The tensor-basis proof is directly reconstructed from P000062--P000063.
present_status: As of November 2026, the statement holds for the standard probability and separability setting; the constant tensor is excluded.

title: Spectral measures of tensor products are convolutions
notes: Product eigenfunctions produce sums of frequencies, and the associated measure is called a product measure.
statement: For \(\mathbb R\)-representations, the scalar spectral measure of \(v\otimes w\) under \(U_t\otimes V_t\) is the pushforward of \(\mu_v\otimes\nu_w\) by \((\lambda,\eta)\mapsto\lambda+\eta\), hence convolution. For \(\mathbb Z\), use multiplication on \(\mathbb T\).
reconstruction: The acting group is the diagonal subgroup and the spectral pushforward is explicit.
fate: The product-representation setting already appears in \citet[Section~3]{bruhat1954induced}, a December 1952 lecture printed in 1954. The pushforward follows by multiplying the two correlation Fourier transforms.
present_status: As of November 2026, the tensor-product formula is established; the measure on the one-dimensional dual is a pushforward, not the raw Cartesian product.

title: Koopman spectra for general group actions
notes: Dynamical systems are extended to arbitrary groups, with irreducible representations replacing scalar eigenvalues.
statement: A measurable probability-preserving action of a locally compact second-countable group \(G\) on a standard probability space gives a unitary Koopman representation. For a type-I group the usual essentially unique irreducible direct-integral decomposition permits a spectral measure-class and multiplicity description. Arbitrary groups require more care; such data are not automatically a complete classification.
reconstruction: Standard measure spaces, continuity and the type-I restriction on the familiar spectral parametrization are supplied.
fate: The distinction between a representation and an action is central to \citet[Introduction and Section~6]{hermlekreidler2023halmos}. \citet[Section~2]{gelfandfomin1952geodesic} already uses irreducible decomposition for the relevant semisimple groups.
present_status: As of November 2026, the representation-theoretic construction is established; the unrestricted classification language needs the type-I and reconstruction qualifications.

title: Ergodic compact-group actions are essentially homogeneous
notes: For a compact group, an ergodic action is described by a homogeneous space.
statement: An ergodic probability-preserving action of a second-countable compact group on a standard probability space is, modulo null sets, its action on \(G/H\) for a closed subgroup \(H\), with invariant quotient Haar probability. Equivariant isomorphism corresponds to conjugacy of stabilizers.
reconstruction: Closed stabilizer, quotient Haar measure and the modulo-null-sets conclusion are supplied.
fate: The homogeneous model is the compact instance of \citet[Remark~6.44(iii)]{hermlekreidler2023halmos}; the stabilizer classification is explicit in \citet[Sections~2--3]{mackey1966virtual}, reviewing the earlier elementary transitive theory.
present_status: As of November 2026, the theorem holds in the measurable standard-space formulation; pointwise transitivity of an arbitrary representative is stronger than required.

title: A finite-support binary group and an uncertain attribution
notes: The notation is a product of copies of \(\mathbb Z/2\), but the elements are said to have finitely many nonzero coordinates; names resembling Gordin and Whitehead appear.
statement: No unique mathematical statement can be extracted: the group described is \(\bigoplus_{\mathbb N}\mathbb Z/2\), while its topology, action and the attributed result are not specified.
fate: Searches combining the names, binary groups, spectra and ergodic actions did not identify an exact theorem; the finite-support/product discrepancy is recorded separately.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fragment remains unidentifiable from the supplied evidence; this does not establish that a mathematical problem is open.

title: Dyadic roots and their compact dual
notes: The dyadic roots of unity are a countable group whose characters form a compact group.
statement: The discrete Prüfer group \(C_{2^\infty}=\mathbb Z[1/2]/\mathbb Z\) is the direct limit of \(C_{2^n}\). Its Pontryagin dual is the inverse limit \(\varprojlim\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z=\mathbb Z_2\), with the compact inverse-limit topology.
reconstruction: Direct-limit and inverse-limit maps are supplied.
fate: The identification is classical and follows directly by restricting a character to each cyclic subgroup: the resulting residues are compatible modulo successive powers of two. No new spectral theorem is asserted.
present_status: As of November 2026, the group and dual are unambiguous once the discrete topology is specified.

title: Unspecified dyadic spectral decomposition
notes: A remark about point and continuous spectra and pieces of functions follows the dyadic group example.
statement: No unique mathematical statement can be extracted: no action, invariant measure or definite decomposition assertion is supplied.
fate: The dyadic-group identification does not determine the spectrum of an unspecified action; no unique publication match was found.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fragment remains unidentifiable from the supplied evidence; this does not establish that a mathematical problem is open.

title: The full real affine group has one infinite-dimensional irreducible
notes: The group \(x\mapsto ax+b\), \(a\ne0\), is said to have one infinite-dimensional irreducible representation, besides characters.
statement: For \(G=\mathbb R\rtimes\mathbb R^\times\), the one-dimensional unitary characters are \((b,a)\mapsto |a|^{it}\operatorname{sgn}(a)^\varepsilon\), \(t\in\mathbb R,\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}\), and there is exactly one infinite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation up to equivalence. Restricting the group to \(a>0\) gives two such irreducibles instead.
reconstruction: The full group, continuous unitary representations and both one-dimensional character parameters are explicit.
fate: \citet[Sections~2.2--2.3 and Section~5]{choighandehari2021affine} explicitly records this classical Mackey classification and distinguishes the connected subgroup.
present_status: As of November 2026, the notebook’s word one is correct for the full group; replacing it by two would silently change the group.

title: Discrete full-group spectrum on a compact hyperbolic quotient
notes: For a compact surface of negative curvature the relevant Lorentz-group representation is said to have discrete spectrum.
statement: Let \(G=PSL(2,\mathbb R)\) and \(\Gamma\) be cocompact discrete. The right representation of \(G\) on \(L^2(\Gamma\backslash G)\) is a discrete Hilbert sum of irreducibles, each with finite multiplicity. Its restriction to the geodesic one-parameter subgroup has Lebesgue spectrum on \(L^2_0\), so the two uses of spectrum must not be identified.
reconstruction: The acting group, cocompactness and the distinction between full-group decomposition and flow spectrum are supplied.
fate: \citet[Sections~2--3, especially p.~132]{gelfandfomin1952geodesic} establishes the continuous-time Lebesgue conclusion. For the full-group discreteness assertion, compactness makes integrated compactly supported continuous kernels compact; the usual compact-operator decomposition supplies the discrete sum.
present_status: As of November 2026, the full-group and one-parameter assertions coexist; compactness alone does not give pure-point geodesic-flow spectrum.

title: Measurable cocycles and coboundaries
notes: Operators have form \(T_gf(x)=f(xg)\chi(x,g)\); equivalent multipliers differ by a ratio of a function at \(xg\) and \(x\).
statement: For a right probability-preserving action, a measurable \(\mathbb T\)-valued cocycle satisfies \(\alpha(x,gh)=\alpha(x,g)\alpha(xg,h)\), almost everywhere with the chosen measurable formulation. It defines unitary \(T_gf(x)=\alpha(x,g)f(xg)\). Replacing \(\alpha\) by \(b(x)^{-1}\alpha(x,g)b(xg)\) conjugates the representation by multiplication by \(b\).
reconstruction: Unit-modulus values, preservation of measure and an explicit right-action convention are supplied.
fate: \citet[Section~5; Russian translation pp.~127--128]{mackey1966virtual} gives the cocycle and cohomology formulas and explains their 1963 announcement.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is established; measurable equivalence and changes on null sets require the standard cocycle framework.

title: Transitive cocycles and stabilizer representations
notes: For a transitive action the cocycle classes are identified with representations of the subgroup.
statement: For the homogeneous right action on \(H\backslash G\), strict Borel cocycles with values in a compact group \(K\), up to Borel cohomology, correspond to continuous homomorphisms \(H\to K\) up to conjugacy. With \(K=\mathbb T\) these are characters of \(H\); with \(K=U(n)\) they are \(n\)-dimensional unitary representations.
reconstruction: Strict Borel representatives, closed stabilizer and the coefficient group are specified.
fate: \citet[Section~5, final transitive-case paragraph]{mackey1966virtual} gives precisely the homomorphism correspondence; \citet[Section~2]{bruhat1954induced} supplies the earlier induced-representation framework.
present_status: As of November 2026, the scalar formula yields characters, while higher-dimensional representations require vector-valued cocycles.

title: Virtual subgroups and ergodic groupoids
notes: Mackey’s generalized subgroups and the analogy between transitive and ergodic actions are discussed.
statement: The identifiable programme replaces a homogeneous action’s stabilizer by a virtual subgroup described through an ergodic measured groupoid. It is a framework for actions, cocycles and induction, not a single unsolved conjecture.
reconstruction: The later groupoid language identifies the programme without assigning every later result to the seminar.
fate: \citet{mackey1963ergodic} announced the programme before this seminar; \citet[Introduction and Sections~9--11]{mackey1966virtual} supplies the systematic explanation and the groupoid formulation.
present_status: As of November 2026, the programme became an established part of measured groupoid and ergodic-action theory; the source contains no uniquely delimited remaining question.

notes: A broad reconstruction question asks whether cohomology determines a system.
statement: No unique mathematical statement can be extracted: the cohomology degree, coefficient object, additional structure to retain and equivalence of systems are unspecified.
fate: Mackey’s cocycle programme and later reconstruction results delimit several inequivalent readings. They do not identify this fragment with a particular modern open problem.

title: Products of eigenfunctions and a symmetric two-cocycle
notes: Products of normalized eigenfunctions differ from the eigenfunction of the product eigenvalue by constants, satisfying a cocycle law.
statement: For an ergodic probability-preserving abelian action, choose unit-modulus eigenfunctions \(f_\lambda\). Then \(f_\lambda f_\mu=c(\lambda,\mu)f_{\lambda\mu}\), with \(c\in\mathbb T\); associativity gives the two-cocycle identity and commutativity gives symmetry. Changing phases changes \(c\) by a coboundary. With pure-point spectrum the eigenvalue subgroup classifies the action; otherwise this describes its Kronecker factor only.
reconstruction: Abelian action, normalized modulus, phase equivalence and the pure-point restriction are supplied.
fate: \citet[Theorem~5.5 and the preceding eigenfunction construction]{hermlekreidler2023halmos} gives a modern precise version of the 1942 Halmos--von Neumann classification. The two-cocycle equations follow directly by associating a triple product.
present_status: As of November 2026, the source construction is correct; full reconstruction requires pure-point spectrum and the standard probability-space setting.

title: Unitary spectrum does not determine even a finite ergodic action
notes: Whether the spectrum determines the system is said to be unclear even for finite groups; Gelfand answers that it does not.
statement: The answer is negative even for transitive finite actions. Let \(G=GL(3,\mathbb F_2)\) act on the seven nonzero vectors of \(\mathbb F_2^3\), and on the seven nonzero covectors by the dual action. The permutation characters coincide, but the \(G\)-sets are not isomorphic. With uniform probability these are ergodic systems with unitarily equivalent Koopman representations.
reconstruction: The seven-point example is supplied as an elementary check, not attributed to the notebook or asserted to be Todd’s exact presentation. The full chapter’s independent finite-action computation checks all \(168\) matrices and the stabilizer obstruction.
fate: \citet[Remark~6.44(iii)]{hermlekreidler2023halmos} records the obstruction already noted by Mackey (1964, Section~3, Remark~2), citing Todd’s 1950 example. The explicit seven-point verification here is editorial: fixed-vector and fixed-covector counts agree by rank equality, while the stabilizer of a vector fixes no nonzero covector.
present_status: As of November 2026, the finite-group question has a negative answer; this is not an open reconstruction problem.

title: The icosahedral rotation group needs a central quotient
notes: The icosahedral rotation group is identified with the unimodular group over five elements.
statement: The orientation-preserving icosahedral group is \(A_5\cong PSL(2,\mathbb F_5)=SL(2,\mathbb F_5)/\{\pm I\}\), of order \(60\). The group \(SL(2,\mathbb F_5)\) itself has order \(120\).
reconstruction: The quotient by the center is supplied.
fate: This is the classical finite-group identification. The immediate order check already forces the central quotient: \(|SL(2,\mathbb F_q)|=q(q^2-1)\), and the center at \(q=5\) has two elements.
present_status: As of November 2026, the missing projective quotient is a faithful mathematical error in the note.

title: Multiplicative observables recover the action
notes: The spectral representation forgets multiplication; a ring of functions with its group action restores the system.
statement: For standard probability spaces, a state-preserving normal unital \(*\)-isomorphism between their commutative \(L^\infty\) algebras that intertwines the group actions gives an isomorphism of measure algebras, hence a spatial conjugacy modulo null sets. Retaining just the \(L^2\) representation discards this multiplicative information.
reconstruction: The algebraic, order/normality and probability-state structure is explicit.
fate: \citet[Section~1.2 and Theorem~4.8]{hermlekreidler2023halmos} makes the reconstruction category explicit through Markov lattice homomorphisms and compact models.
present_status: As of November 2026, the structured observable algebra is sufficient in the stated category; an abstract spectrum alone is not.

title: Ergodic eigenfunctions have constant modulus
notes: The notes give \(U_t f_\lambda=e^{i\lambda t}f_\lambda\) and \ru{пост. по mod (у эргод. системы)}.
statement: Let \((X,\mu)\) be a probability space and \((T_t)\) an ergodic measure-preserving measurable flow. If \(0\ne f\in L^2(\mu)\) and \(f\circ T_t=e^{it\lambda}f\) for every \(t\), as equalities in \(L^2\), then \(|f|=c>0\) almost everywhere. More generally the same statement holds for an ergodic action and a unitary character.
reconstruction: The probability-space convention and almost-everywhere qualification make the shorthand precise.
fate: This is an immediate consequence of ergodicity: \(|f|\) is invariant. It is used explicitly, in the normalization \(|f|=1\), by \citet[p.~775]{stepin1966spectra}. That 1966 use is corroboration, not a claim that the elementary observation originated then.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: When is a universal enveloping algebra primitive?
notes: The notes ask when \(U(L)\) is primitive and explain this as admitting a faithful irreducible module; Harish-Chandra and Jacobson are named.
statement: For a specified Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) over a field \(k\), determine whether \(U(\mathfrak g)\) has a faithful simple left module. For finite-dimensional complex \(\mathfrak g\), the Dixmier--Moeglin equivalence gives a precise criterion: the zero ideal is primitive if and only if the center of the quotient division ring of \(U(\mathfrak g)\) is \(\mathbb C\). The restriction on the field and dimension is essential to the stated scope.
reconstruction: Finite dimension, characteristic zero and the base field are not recorded; the complex finite-dimensional case is a reconstruction. No claim is made that all \(U(\mathfrak g)\) are primitive.
fate: \citet[p.~2020]{bell2017poisson} explicitly records the primitive--rational--locally-closed equivalence for enveloping algebras of finite-dimensional complex Lie algebras, crediting Dixmier (1977) and Moeglin (1980). Applied to the zero prime ideal, it yields the criterion stated here. This later primary account was read; the original proofs were not. \citet{ooms1974primitive} is a separate, inaccessible lead on solvable Lie algebras and is not needed to certify the criterion.
present_status: As of November 2026: the finite-dimensional complex problem belongs to an established primitive-ideal theory and admits the stated criterion. The notebook omits the field and dimension, so an unrestricted field-independent classification is not asserted.

title: Two two-dimensional examples of primitive envelopes
notes: The nonabelian relation is \([e_1,e_2]=e_1\); its envelope is called primitive. The abelian two-generator envelope is said not to be primitive because a commutative primitive ring is a field.
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), the two-dimensional nonabelian Lie algebra \([x,h]=x\) has primitive enveloping algebra. In contrast \(U(\mathbb C^2)=\mathbb C[x,h]\) is not primitive: every simple module of a commutative ring is a residue field, and faithfulness forces the ring itself to be a field.
reconstruction: The faithful simple module is an editorial verification, not a reconstruction of an omitted notebook proof. The base field is fixed to \(\mathbb C\).
fate: The nonabelian case can be checked directly on \(\mathbb C[t]\): let \(h\) multiply by \(t\) and \(x f(t)=f(t+1)\), so \([x,h]=x\). A submodule is an ideal stable under translation, hence is zero or the whole ring; distinct finite translations are linearly independent over \(\mathbb C[t]\), giving faithfulness. This elementary verification agrees with the later primitive-ideal framework \citep[p.~2020]{bell2017poisson}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Associative simplicity does not eliminate Lie ideals
notes: Under the name Baxter the manuscript says \ru{Если A --- простая, то Ли-ид. тоже нет}, and repeats that absence of ordinary ideals implies absence of Lie ideals.
statement: The literal assertion is false. In the simple associative algebra \(M_2(\mathbb C)\), the center \(\mathbb C I\) is a proper nonzero Lie ideal; so is \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\). Correct simplicity theorems concern specified commutator Lie algebras, quotients by their centers, or skew elements of an algebra with involution, with characteristic and small-dimension exceptions.
reconstruction: The corrected theorem is intentionally not guessed: the notebook omits the quotient or involution that would determine which result was intended.
fate: Baxter\textquotesingle s paper \citet[title and theorem scope]{baxter1956lie} concerns a special class of associative rings; its topic cannot validate the unrestricted sentence. The direct matrix counterexamples already settle the literal reading. No new open problem is inferred from the error.
present_status: As of November 2026: false literally; the intended Baxter theorem remains incompletely identified.

title: Uniform nilpotence on a generating Lie algebra
notes: The Burnside/Kostrikin paragraph has finite generators \(X\), their Lie algebra \([X]\), and a corrected quantifier \(\exists n\) followed by \(e^n=0\). It concludes that the associative algebra is \ru{нильпот.}, glossed as every element being nilpotent.
statement: The strongest recoverable question is: if a finitely generated associative algebra \(A\) over an unspecified field is generated by a finite set \(X\), and every element of the Lie subalgebra generated by \(X\) has a common associative nilpotence bound, what follows about \(A\)? Being nil (each element nilpotent) and being nilpotent (\(A^m=0\) for one \(m\)) are different conclusions.
reconstruction: The membership sign \(e\in[X]\) and universal quantification over \(e\) are interpretive expansions. The field, associativity and distinction between nil and nilpotent are not supplied by the notes.
fate: Searches on Latyshev, Kostrikin, the restricted Burnside problem, Lie-generated associative algebras and bounded nilpotence did not identify a theorem with precisely these assumptions and conclusion. A citation to a restricted-Burnside theorem alone would not supply the omitted characteristic and identity hypotheses.
present_status: As of November 2026: insufficiently specified for a reliable fate assignment; not classified as an undeveloped conjecture.

title: Weyl algebras of different ranks
notes: The two rings are written \(P(x,d/dx)\) and \(P(x,d/dx,y,d/dy)\), followed by \ru{Изоморфны ли эти кольца?}.
statement: Over a field \(k\) of characteristic zero, let \(A_n(k)\) be the unital associative \(k\)-algebra generated by \(x_1,\ldots,x_n,\partial_1,\ldots,\partial_n\), with relations \[ [x_i,x_j]=[\partial_i,\partial_j]=0,\qquad [\partial_i,x_j]=\delta_{ij}1\quad(1\le i,j\le n). \] Are \(A_1(k)\) and \(A_2(k)\) isomorphic as \(k\)-algebras? They are not: more generally, \(A_m(k)\cong A_n(k)\) implies \(m=n\).
reconstruction: The base field and preservation of it are made explicit. The scan decisively shows one canonical pair versus two.
fate: \citet[\S4, Lemma~5 and Theorem~2, pp.~11--14]{gelfandkirillov1966corps} distinguish the algebras \(R_{n,k}\), including Weyl algebras, by growth. The paper was received 19 January 1966 and published that year. In modern terms \(\operatorname{GKdim}A_n=2n\). This is unrelated in quantifiers to asking whether every endomorphism of one fixed \(A_n\) is an automorphism.
present_status: As of November 2026: solved negatively for isomorphism of distinct ranks; the same-year first index must not label this an open fixed-rank endomorphism conjecture.

title: The circular orthogonal ensemble as U(N)/O(N)
notes: Symmetric unitary matrices satisfy \(U^T=U\), \(UU^*=I\), with action \(U\mapsto VUV^T\); the stabilizer at the identity is orthogonal. The eigenangle density has Vandermonde power one.
statement: The pushforward of Haar measure under \(V\mapsto VV^T\) on \(U(N)\) is the invariant probability measure on \(U(N)/O(N)\). Its unordered eigenangles have joint density \(Z_{N,1}^{-1}\prod_{i<j}|e^{i\theta_i}-e^{i\theta_j}|\) relative to Lebesgue measure on \([0,2\pi)^N\), with the ordering convention absorbed in \(Z_{N,1}\).
fate: This is Dyson\textquotesingle s circular orthogonal ensemble, published in 1962 after receipt in September 1961; see \citet[the circular ensembles and eigenvalue measures]{dyson1962statisticalI}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Haar unitary eigenangles and quadratic repulsion
notes: For all unitary matrices the notes display Vandermonde power two and discuss integration over conjugacy classes. In the action formula the final \(V^*\) is crossed or omitted.
statement: For Haar-distributed \(U\in U(N)\), the eigenangle density is \(Z_{N,2}^{-1}\prod_{i<j}|e^{i\theta_i}-e^{i\theta_j}|^2\). Haar invariance is under left and right multiplication; conjugation \(U\mapsto VUV^*\) is the action relevant to eigenvalue class integration.
reconstruction: Left invariance and conjugacy invariance are separated instead of treating the incomplete action as a new ensemble.
fate: The circular unitary ensemble and its eigenangle law are already in \citet[unitary ensemble]{dyson1962statisticalI}. Coinciding angles have vanishing density, the precise content of the recorded repulsion remark.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Circular beta gap integrals and logarithmic interaction
notes: The forbidden arc is \((-\alpha,\alpha)\); the normalized probability is eventually written \(R_\beta=\Psi_\beta(\alpha)/\Psi_\beta(0)\). The first energy sign conflicts with the later Boltzmann factor.
statement: For \(N\ge1,\beta>0,0\le\alpha<\pi\), define \(\Psi_{N,\beta}(\alpha)=\int_{[\alpha,2\pi-\alpha]^N}\prod_{i<j}|e^{i\theta_i}-e^{i\theta_j}|^\beta\,d\theta\). Then \(R_{N,\beta}(\alpha)=\Psi_{N,\beta}(\alpha)/\Psi_{N,\beta}(0)\) is the no-eigenangle probability. With energy \(W=-\sum_{i<j}\log|e^{i\theta_i}-e^{i\theta_j}|\), the density is proportional to \(e^{-\beta W}\).
reconstruction: The sign convention, product over pairs and normalization are supplied explicitly; \(\beta>0\) is a sufficient integrability range, not the maximal possible range.
fate: Dyson\textquotesingle s log-gas construction is exact at the finite integral level; see \citet[statistical-mechanical interpretation]{dyson1962statisticalI}. The source\textquotesingle s missing product and normalization are repaired by its own next page.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Continuum density and local free-energy approximation
notes: The notes replace the point density by \(\sigma\), impose \(\int\sigma=N\), and write \(F=V+F_1\) with a logarithmic double integral and a local term \(\int\sigma f_\beta(\sigma)\). They label the construction a physical assumption.
statement: The empirical measure is \(\sum_{j=1}^N\delta_{\theta_j}\), not an ordinary density. A continuum ansatz replaces it by \(\sigma(\theta)\,d\theta\), minimizes a logarithmic-energy functional under the mass and support constraints, and adds a local entropy correction. This does not give an exact finite-\(N\) theorem. If \(F=-\beta^{-1}\log\Psi\), then \(R=e^{-\beta(F_\alpha-F_0)}\).
reconstruction: The distinction between an empirical measure and a density, and between an ansatz and a theorem, is editorial. The source also permits its positive-sign exponential to define an opposite convention for \(F\); it cannot simultaneously be the usual minimized free energy without a sign change.
fate: The method is the 1962 Dyson asymptotic program, not an independently established exact identity. Later determinant asymptotics such as \citet[Introduction and the large-gap formulas]{ehrhardt2007dyson} separate leading energy, logarithmic terms and constants.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The cosine-power expression is not an exact CUE gap probability
notes: The manuscript writes \(R_2(\alpha)=\exp(N^2\log\cos(\alpha/2))\) as an equality.
statement: The equality \(R_{N,2}(\alpha)=\cos(\alpha/2)^{N^2}\) is false for the stated circular unitary ensemble. For \(N=1\), the eigenangle is uniform and \(R_{1,2}(\alpha)=1-\alpha/\pi\), which is not \(\cos(\alpha/2)\). The cosine-power captures a leading energy contribution in an appropriate large-\(N\) regime, not the complete finite probability.
reconstruction: The one-eigenvalue check is an editorial diagnosis. No unrecorded special ensemble is inserted to save the equality.
fate: The later asymptotic theory includes essential subleading powers and constants. \citet[Introduction]{ehrhardt2007dyson} verifies the distinction in the sine-kernel limit; it is not a proof of the notebook\textquotesingle s finite equality. The same expression returns in item 1964-42.1.
present_status: As of November 2026: the finite identity is disproved by \(N=1\); precise large-gap asymptotics are established.

title: Frobenius fixed points and the cohomological counting program
notes: Reduction modulo \(p\) is denoted \(Z_p\). Over its algebraic closure, \(x\mapsto x^p\) fixes exactly the base field; a Lefschetz alternating trace is proposed to count rational points.
statement: For a finite-type scheme \(X/\mathbb F_q\), \(X(\mathbb F_q)\) is the fixed-point set of the geometric Frobenius action on geometric points. The precise cohomological formula is \(\#X(\mathbb F_q)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(\operatorname{Frob}_q\mid H^i_c(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},\mathbb Q_\ell))\), with \(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}\mathbb F_q\) and compatible Frobenius convention.
reconstruction: Finite type, compact supports, \(\ell\)-adic coefficients and the Frobenius convention are later precise reconstruction, not statements supplied in the notes.
fate: The notebook describes the Weil--Grothendieck program rather than a usable topological Lefschetz theorem in the Zariski topology. The étale-site framework was circulating in the 1963--64 SGA seminar; the published source is \citet[Exposés I--IV, site and topos foundations]{sga4I1972}. The full trace formula requires additional étale-cohomological finiteness and trace theorems.
present_status: As of November 2026: the arithmetic trace formula is established; the recorded ordinary-topological analogy alone is insufficient.

title: Slice categories and relative products
notes: The objects over \(X\) are arrows \(U\to X\); a morphism is a commuting triangle. The universal property of products is explained, with open-set intersection and pairs having the same image as examples.
statement: For a category \(\mathcal C\), the slice \(\mathcal C/X\) has objects \(U\to X\). If \(U\times_X V\) exists, it is the product of \(U\to X\) and \(V\to X\) in this slice. Its universal property gives uniqueness up to a unique isomorphism. For the poset of opens of a space, this is intersection.
fate: This is the categorical language used in SGA~4; see \citet[Exposé I]{sga4I1972} and the explicit modern site conventions of \citet[Tag 00VH]{stacks2026sites}. Publication in 1972 must not be mistaken for first circulation: the seminar dates to 1963--64.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Covering families and Grothendieck topologies
notes: The axioms require identity coverings, composition of covering families and preservation under pullback. Existence of every pairwise product in the slice is recorded separately.
statement: A pretopology on a category with the requisite fiber products is a collection of covering families containing isomorphisms and stable under base change and composition. It generates a Grothendieck topology of covering sieves. A general Grothendieck topology does not require all fiber products in the underlying category; the notes use a convenient stronger presentation.
reconstruction: The distinction between a pretopology of families and a topology of sieves is modern clarification.
fate: This is established pre-lecture Grothendieck-site theory, circulated in SGA~4 (1963--64) and published in \citet[Exposé II]{sga4I1972}. \citet[Tag 00VH and covering axioms]{stacks2026sites} supplies a checked current formulation.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Sheaf descent and the point represented by a field
notes: A presheaf is a contravariant abelian-group-valued functor. Compatible sections over a covering glue uniquely. The notes add that a point can mean a field and then give Galois cohomology.
statement: A sheaf \(F\) on a site with fiber products satisfies the equalizer condition \(F(U)\to\prod_iF(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F(U_i\times_U U_j)\). On the small étale site of \(\operatorname{Spec}k\), abelian sheaves correspond to discrete continuous modules for \(G_k=\operatorname{Gal}(k^{\mathrm{sep}}/k)\); sheaf cohomology identifies with continuous Galois cohomology.
reconstruction: The small étale topology and continuity of the Galois action are missing but decisive hypotheses.
fate: See \citet[Exposé II]{sga4I1972} for the foundations and \citet[Tags 00VL and 03QR]{stacks2026sites} for descent and the field case. The Zariski site of a one-point space would not produce this Galois information.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Subjects proposed for study
notes: The list includes Lie groups and representations, sheaves and homological algebra, bundles, algebraic geometry, quantum mechanics, several-variable Cauchy theory and nuclear spaces with measures.
statement: This is a curriculum proposal, not a theorem or a mathematically quantified research problem.
fate: No publication fate can be assigned to a list of study topics. Its value is evidence of the seminar\textquotesingle s program and links to records 39, 40, 48 and 49.
present_status: As of November 2026: historical planning evidence; no open mathematical status is applicable.

title: Dyson-type calculations on symmetric spaces
notes: Gelfand proposes investigating Dyson\textquotesingle s results for general symmetric spaces.
statement: One precise direction is to push invariant measure on a specified compact symmetric space to a maximal flat and compute the Jacobian in restricted-root coordinates, then study eigenvalue or radial gap observables. A space, normalization, root multiplicities and observable must be specified before an exact theorem can be stated.
reconstruction: The restricted-root formulation and choice of radial observables are an explanatory modern realization, not an assertion that the notebook posed a complete classification problem.
fate: Dyson\textquotesingle s \(U(N)/O(N)\) example is already a compact symmetric space \citep{dyson1962statisticalI}. Later random-matrix symmetry classifications systematically use symmetric spaces \citep[the symmetry-class correspondence]{altlandzirnbauer1997}. This matches the direction, not a single universal gap formula.
present_status: As of November 2026: extensively developed as a framework; the short suggestion is too broad to carry an unresolved problem label.

title: Repeated cosine-power claim and an unnamed replacement model
notes: The speaker says the cosine-power result has not been proved for the original model but another similar model gives it exactly. That replacement model is not specified.
statement: For the original finite circular unitary ensemble, the asserted exact identity is false as in item 1964-39.5. No exact alternative statement can be recovered without the replacement ensemble and its probability measure.
fate: Dyson\textquotesingle s asymptotic program and subsequent sine-kernel work explain the leading exponential, but do not identify the unrecorded substitute ensemble \citep[Introduction]{ehrhardt2007dyson}. The two claims must be separated: a false literal finite-CUE equality and an unidentifiable possible exact identity for another model.
present_status: As of November 2026: the original equality is false; the unnamed model remains unidentified. This is not evidence of an open exact-CUE problem.

title: Nearest-neighbor spacing from the empty-interval probability
notes: A translation-invariant two-endpoint expression is written as \(S(\theta_2-\theta_1)\), and the spacing density is related to a second derivative of the empty-interval probability.
statement: For a stationary simple point process on \(\mathbb R\) of intensity \(\rho>0\), let \(E(s)=\Pr\{N(0,s)=0\}\). Under the usual differentiability assumptions, the density \(p(s)\) of the forward nearest-neighbor distance under the Palm law is \(p(s)=E^{\prime\prime}(s)/\rho\). At unit intensity this is \(p=E^{\prime\prime}\). If the gap is parameterized by a half-width, chain-rule factors must also be included.
reconstruction: The Palm nearest-neighbor law, intensity and differentiability hypotheses identify precisely which spacing distribution is meant.
fate: This is the standard gap-to-spacing mechanism in Dyson\textquotesingle s statistical theory \citep[spacing distributions]{dyson1962statisticalIII}. The notebook omits the density normalization; a two-point correlation function is not in general a nearest-neighbor density.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Even sine-kernel determinant and the large-gap exponent
notes: The finite matrix is \(\delta_{pq}-\pi^{-1}\int_{-\alpha}^{\alpha}\cos(p\theta)\cos(q\theta)\,d\theta\), with half-integer \(p,q\). The scan shows an asymptotic factor \(t^{17/8}e^{-t^2/4-t/2}\) and \(t=\alpha n\).
statement: For \(K_+(x,y)=\sin(x-y)/(\pi(x-y))+\sin(x+y)/(\pi(x+y))\) on \(L^2(0,s)\), the established asymptotic is \(\log\det(I-K_+)=-s^2/4-s/2-(1/8)\log s+c_++o(1)\) as \(s\to\infty\). Thus the power in this standard normalization is \(-1/8\), not \(17/8\).
reconstruction: The continuum kernel is identified separately from the finite matrix. The power is a faithful manuscript error, while the exact \(m,n,t\) normalization remains an ambiguity; no silent rescaling is made.
fate: \citet[Introduction, formulas for \(K_\pm\)]{ehrhardt2007dyson} proves the large-gap constant as well as the displayed terms (preprint April 2006; publication 2007). The finite cosine matrix is a precursor of this even kernel. The manuscript relation between \(2m\) and \(n\) is itself uncertain (equality or inequality); the natural continuum scaling of the matrix uses \(m\alpha\). The source\textquotesingle s \(t=\alpha n\) is therefore not silently identified with the standard \(s\).
present_status: As of November 2026: the standard even-kernel asymptotic is established; the manuscript power and unexplained scaling cannot be used literally.

title: Continuous spectral component for a dyadic torsion-group action
notes: The group is the dyadic rationals modulo one; the generators satisfy \(T_{1/2^{k+1}}^2=T_{1/2^k}\). The notes describe rearrangements of interval pieces and claim a continuous spectral component.
statement: There is an ergodic probability-preserving action of the discrete Prüfer group \(\mathbb Z[1/2]/\mathbb Z\) whose Koopman representation has a nonzero continuous spectral component, although each individual group element has finite order. Continuous means non-atomic spectral measure on the compact dual group, not continuous time and not necessarily Lebesgue measure.
reconstruction: The discrete topology on the group, joint spectral measure and distinction between continuous and absolutely continuous spectrum are made explicit.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~774--776]{stepin1966spectra} constructs precisely this group action on a circle times a two-point space. Its even subspace has discrete spectrum; its odd subspace has simple singular continuous spectrum. The paper was presented 23 November 1965 and published in 1966.
present_status: As of November 2026: the announced construction and its singular-continuous refinement are established.

title: Central section volumes determine an origin-symmetric body
notes: The body is explicitly centrally symmetric. In three dimensions the notes replace it by \(\rho^2/2\) on \(S^2\) and invoke spherical harmonics to invert integration over great circles.
statement: If \(K,L\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(n\ge2\), are origin-symmetric star bodies with positive continuous radial functions and \(\operatorname{vol}_{n-1}(K\cap u^\perp)=\operatorname{vol}_{n-1}(L\cap u^\perp)\) for all \(u\in S^{n-1}\), then \(K=L\). The section function is the spherical Radon transform of \(\rho_K^{n-1}/(n-1)\); the transform is injective on even functions. In \(n=3\), its spherical-harmonic multiplier at degree \(2j\) is \(2\pi P_{2j}(0)\ne0\), while odd degrees are killed.
reconstruction: Origin symmetry, continuous star bodies and the \((n-1)\)-dimensional measure generalize the explicit three-dimensional argument. Convexity is sufficient but not needed.
fate: The great-circle transform is classical Funk theory, originating before the seminar \citep{funk1913flachen}. The modern geometric formulation is documented by \citet[section functions and geometric tomography]{gardner2026tomography}. The original Funk publication metadata was checked; the general-dimensional formulation is a modern reconstruction.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Do all projection areas determine a convex body?
notes: The final question asks whether the areas of all shadows determine the convex body, followed only by \ru{Сводится}.
statement: For \(n\ge2\), the brightness function \(b_K(u)=\operatorname{vol}_{n-1}(K\mid u^\perp)\) determines an origin-symmetric convex body \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) uniquely among such bodies. Without a fixed center, translation is invisible; without central symmetry, uniqueness fails, already because \(K\) and \(-K\) have the same brightness.
reconstruction: The inherited central-symmetry assumption is made explicit; if the last line is read independently for arbitrary convex bodies, its affirmative answer is false.
fate: Aleksandrov\textquotesingle s projection theorem dates to 1937; the precise symmetric uniqueness statement and date are given by \citet[Reconstruction from brightness functions; reference to Theorem~3.3.1]{gardner2026tomography}. This is an old theorem under the symmetry convention of the preceding paragraph, not an unresolved projection problem.
present_status: As of November 2026: affirmative with origin symmetry, negative as an unrestricted uniqueness claim.

title: Dvoretzky almost-Euclidean sections
notes: For every \(\varepsilon,k\), a sufficiently high-dimensional centrally symmetric convex body has a \(k\)-dimensional section that is nearly a ball.
statement: For every \(k\ge1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), there is \(N(k,\varepsilon)\) such that every real normed space of dimension at least \(N\) has a \(k\)-dimensional subspace \(E\), a Euclidean norm \(|\cdot|\) on \(E\), and \(a>0\) with \(a|x|\le\|x\|\le(1+\varepsilon)a|x|\) for all \(x\in E\). The corresponding ellipsoid comparison is affine, not a demand for a round section in an arbitrarily fixed ambient metric.
reconstruction: The norm comparison fixes the quantitative meaning of nearly a ball and allows a suitable Euclidean structure.
fate: Dvoretzky\textquotesingle s result appeared in the proceedings of the 1960 Jerusalem symposium, published in 1961. \citet[p.~297, stated theorem]{figiel1976dvoretzky} gives a later short proof and identifies that original publication.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: A sphere-bundle and low-harmonic vanishing proposal
notes: The fiber consists of a unit vector in a \(k\)-plane. The notes claim that, for large \(n\), some fiber kills the first \(\ell\) nonconstant spherical components, then state a broader unitary-representation version. A condition on outer-to-inner radii is left unfinished; weaker and stronger appear in adjacent comments.
statement: The incidence space \(M_{n,k}=\{(E,v):E\in G_k(\mathbb R^n),v\in E,|v|=1\}\) has fiber \(S^{k-1}\). A precise possible question concerns simultaneous vanishing of specified nonconstant harmonic projections of the restriction of a norm to one fiber. The notebook does not specify the representation, parity, regularity, dimension bounds or extra convex-body condition needed to turn its universal sentence into a theorem.
reconstruction: The corrected fiber dimension is certain. A conjectural completion of the harmonic assertion would be editorial invention and is not supplied.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1]{gromov1967banach}, received September 1966 and published 1967, proves results on normed spaces whose subspaces are mutually isometric. Its theorem is not the exact harmonic-vanishing assertion recorded here. Searches of the paper and the Dvoretzky/Grassmannian literature did not establish an exact match.
present_status: As of November 2026: the program is recognizable, but this particular theorem announcement remains unidentified; no claim of an orphan open problem is made.

title: Hermitian matrix Brownian motion and eigenvalue diffusion
notes: The notes say only that the Hermitian matrix entries are Gaussian random variables and then \ru{Брауновское дв-ние}.
statement: A standard realization takes independent real Brownian diagonal entries of variance \(dt\) and independent complex off-diagonal entries with real and imaginary variances \(dt/2\), reflected by Hermitian symmetry. Starting with distinct eigenvalues, its eigenvalues satisfy \(d\lambda_i=dB_i+\sum_{j\ne i}(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)^{-1}dt\) up to, and in fact without, collision. Other entry normalizations rescale time.
reconstruction: The independent increments, variances and stochastic equation are the modern reconstruction. A single Gaussian matrix does not determine a time process.
fate: Dyson\textquotesingle s Brownian-motion model was published in 1962 \citep{dyson1962brownian}. The title and metadata match this interpretation, but the short fragment itself does not distinguish free matrix Brownian motion from a Gaussian stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck variant.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Angles between two k-dimensional subspaces
notes: The question is simply what an angle between two \(k\)-dimensional subspaces in \(n\) dimensions means.
statement: For subspaces \(E,F\) of a Euclidean or complex Hermitian space, with orthonormal column matrices \(Q_E,Q_F\), the singular values of \(Q_E^*Q_F\) are \(\cos\theta_1,\ldots,\cos\theta_r\), where \(r=\min(\dim E,\dim F)\) and \(0\le\theta_1\le\cdots\le\theta_r\le\pi/2\). These principal angles, including forced zeros from intersections, describe the relative position up to ambient isometry.
reconstruction: The notes ask for an angle; the answer is generally a list of principal angles. The complex version and matrix expression are added for precision.
fate: The theory goes back to \citet[\S\S IV--V; introduction, pp.~104--105]{jordan1875geometrie}, presented in May 1875. The singular-value expression is modern notation for this established collection of invariants.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Finite-interval characteristic function and resolvent trace
notes: For \(L=-d^2/dx^2+q\) on \([0,\pi]\) with Neumann ends, \(\psi(0,\lambda)=1\), \(\psi_x(0,\lambda)=0\), and \(w(\lambda)=\psi_x(\pi,\lambda)\). The finite-matrix identity \(d\log w/d\lambda=-\operatorname{Tr}(L-\lambda)^{-1}\) is proposed.
statement: For real \(q\in L^1(0,\pi)\) and the self-adjoint Neumann realization, \(w\) is entire, with zeros exactly the simple eigenvalues. Outside the spectrum, \(w^{\prime}(\lambda)/w(\lambda)=-\operatorname{Tr}(L-\lambda)^{-1}\). The derivative on \(w\) is with respect to \(\lambda\); the derivative on \(\psi\) is spatial. Multiplying \(w\) by a nonzero constant leaves the identity unchanged.
reconstruction: Integrability, real potential, operator domain and the two different derivatives are made explicit.
fate: This is classical one-dimensional spectral theory. The determinant-to-solution method belongs to the pre-seminar scattering and inverse-spectral framework of \citet[\S\S1--2]{faddeev1959inverse}; the finite-interval formula itself follows from the Green kernel and Lagrange identity. It is not a newly announced 1965 result.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Half-line Jost function as a relative determinant
notes: On the half-line, with \(y(0)=0\) and rapidly decaying \(q\), the resolvent has no ordinary trace. A free part is subtracted; the outgoing solution satisfies \(f(x,k)\sim e^{ikx}\), and \(W(\lambda)=f(0,\sqrt\lambda)\).
statement: For real \(q\) with \(\int_0^\infty(1+x)|q(x)|\,dx<\infty\), take the Dirichlet Schrödinger operator \(H\), free operator \(H_0\), and \(k^2=z\) with \(\operatorname{Im}k>0\). The normalized perturbation determinant is the Jost value \(D(z)=f(0,k)\); off both spectra, \(-d\log D/dz=\operatorname{Tr}((H-z)^{-1}-(H_0-z)^{-1})\). The difference, not the individual resolvent, is trace class.
reconstruction: The relative normalization \(D=1\) for \(q=0\) and a sufficient short-range hypothesis are supplied. The scribbled diagonal asymptotic alone does not justify trace class.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1, p.~13]{buslaevfaddeev1960traces} gives the identity between the relative resolvent trace and the logarithmic derivative of the Jost function before the seminar; the note was received 17 December 1959 and published in 1960. Jost solutions are developed in \citet[\S1 and \S6]{faddeev1959inverse}. The precise Fredholm-determinant equality under weaker \(L^1\) conditions is also verified in \citet[Theorem~1.1]{gesztesy2007jost}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Resolvent sheets and free Green kernels
notes: The notes discuss square-root branching in one dimension and logarithmic branching in two, and say one must leave the Hilbert-space setting to see a multivalued resolvent.
statement: The bounded-operator resolvent \((H-z)^{-1}\) is single-valued and analytic on its resolvent set. For the free one-dimensional operator, its outgoing kernel is \(i e^{ik|x-y|}/(2k)\), \(k^2=z,\operatorname{Im}k>0\), so the kernel has a continuation in the square-root parameter. In two dimensions the outgoing Hankel kernel has logarithmic branching. Continuation across continuous spectrum requires specified weighted spaces or compactly supported test functions.
reconstruction: The distinction between the physical resolvent and continued kernels is essential; no general meromorphic continuation is asserted for every decaying potential.
fate: This interpretation agrees with the analytic scattering framework in \citet[\S\S1--2]{faddeev1959inverse}. It corrects a possible literal reading that an abstract Hilbert-space resolvent is multivalued on its ordinary domain.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Whole-line Jost Wronskian
notes: Two solutions behave like \(e^{ikx}\) at plus infinity and \(e^{-ikx}\) at minus infinity. Their Wronskian \(f_1^{\prime} f_2-f_1 f_2^{\prime}\) is called the determinant.
statement: For real short-range \(q\) on \(\mathbb R\), let \(f_\pm(x,k)\sim e^{\pm ikx}\) at \(\pm\infty\), with \(\operatorname{Im}k>0\). The Wronskian \(W(k)=f_+^{\prime} f_- - f_+f_-^{\prime}\) is independent of \(x\); its zeros in the upper half-plane give bound states, with the usual threshold caveat at \(k=0\). The free Wronskian is \(2ik\), so a relative determinant uses \(W(k)/(2ik)\).
reconstruction: The short-range assumption may be taken as \(\int_{\mathbb R}(1+|x|)|q|<\infty\). The normalization and threshold exception are editorial additions.
fate: The construction belongs to the pre-1965 inverse-scattering theory; \citet[whole-line extensions in the introduction and supplementary remarks]{faddeev1959inverse} distinguishes these extensions from the main half-line problem. The unnormalized Wronskian is a characteristic function, not automatically a normalized Fredholm determinant.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Argument principle and analytically regularized spectral sums
notes: The notes integrate \(h(\lambda)W^{\prime}(\lambda)/W(\lambda)\), deform the contour, and use \(h=\lambda^s\). The real-axis expression is followed by the annotation that the integral is a jump.
statement: If \(W\) is meromorphic and nonzero on a closed contour and \(h\) is analytic inside it, \((2\pi i)^{-1}\oint hW^{\prime}/W\) equals the zero sum minus the pole sum, with multiplicities. A deformation onto a cut must retain both boundary values, its orientation and the factor \((2\pi i)^{-1}\). For spectral zeta or trace identities, convergence, subtraction of asymptotic terms and continuation must be proved separately.
reconstruction: The argument-principle statement is exact; its application to an unspecified spectral determinant and branch of \(\lambda^s\) remains conditional.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~14--15]{buslaevfaddeev1960traces} carries out contour deformation, asymptotic subtraction and Mellin continuation in the singular Sturm--Liouville setting. Its finite-interval discussion on p.~16 uses Dirichlet ends, so it is not silently identified with the notebook\textquotesingle s Neumann expression. This is pre-seminar trace theory, not a universal ordinary-integral identity.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: An unidentified boundary term in a Neumann regularized trace
notes: The scan reads \(\sum_n(\lambda_n-n^2-c_0)=\tfrac14(y^{\prime}(0)-y^{\prime}(\pi))\). No function \(y\) on that right side is defined.
statement: A standard comparison, for a sufficiently smooth real potential and Neumann eigenvalues numbered \(\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\ldots\), is \(\sum_{n=0}^\infty(\lambda_n-n^2-\bar q)=(q(0)+q(\pi))/4-\bar q/2\), where \(\bar q=\pi^{-1}\int_0^\pi q\). This is a different, specified statement; it cannot identify the written \(y^{\prime}\)-difference without an additional definition.
reconstruction: The comparison formula is supplied to expose the ambiguity; it is not silently substituted into the transcription.
fate: The Gelfand--Levitan trace identity dates to 1953, followed by Gelfand\textquotesingle s 1956 treatment \citep{gelfand1956identities}. The recorded boundary expression is therefore classified as an unidentified or corrupted instance of established trace theory, not a new spectral formula.
present_status: As of November 2026: the regularized-trace theory is established, but this exact boundary expression cannot be recovered from the notes.

title: Formal diagonal kernels and boundary contributions
notes: The distributional kernel \(-\delta^{\prime\prime}(x-y)+q(x)\delta(x-y)\) is restricted formally to the diagonal. The notes write \(\delta(0)=0\), then discuss a boundary coefficient \(1/4\).
statement: The distribution \(\delta(x-y)\) has no pointwise diagonal value \(\delta(0)\), and multiplication by a nonzero potential is not trace class on \(L^2\). A valid regularized trace must first specify a spectral, heat-kernel or resolvent subtraction and account for its endpoint terms. The displayed manipulations are heuristic motivation, not legitimate distributional equalities.
reconstruction: The source\textquotesingle s distinction between periodic and endpoint problems is retained as motivation, while the regularization is not invented.
fate: The endpoint effects belong to established regularized-trace formulas \citep{gelfand1956identities,buslaevfaddeev1960traces}. Their rigorous existence does not validate the intermediate assertion \(\delta(0)=0\).
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: When does a commutator have trace zero?
notes: Gelfand writes \(\operatorname{Sp}(AB-BA)=0\) and labels it a problem, without operator-ideal assumptions.
statement: For bounded operators on a Hilbert space, \(\operatorname{Tr}(AB)=\operatorname{Tr}(BA)\) when both products are trace class (in particular if one factor is trace class). Merely requiring \([A,B]\) to be trace class is insufficient: for the unilateral shift \(S\) on \(\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\), \([S^*,S]=P_{e_0}\) has trace one.
reconstruction: The two distinct hypotheses are separated. The rank-one shift example is an explicit diagnosis of the unrestricted formulation.
fate: The question depends completely on the trace domain. Nonzero traces of trace-class commutators became a substantial theory; \citet[Introduction]{heltonhowe1975traces} develops trace formulas for almost commuting operators and relates them to symbols and index theory. This is a later development, not evidence for the unrestricted zero-trace assertion.
present_status: As of November 2026: vanishing is established in the standard trace-cyclicity domain and false under the weaker trace-class-commutator assumption.

title: Product Cauchy formula and analytic polyhedra
notes: A bicylinder \(D_z\times D_w\) has the iterated Cauchy formula. Weil domains are cut out by holomorphic \(\chi_i(z,w)\in D_i\).
statement: If \(D_1,D_2\subset\mathbb C\) have piecewise smooth positively oriented boundaries and \(f\) is holomorphic near \(\overline{D_1\times D_2}\), then \(f(z,w)=(2\pi i)^{-2}\int_{\partial D_1\times\partial D_2}f(\zeta,\eta)\,d\zeta\wedge d\eta/((\zeta-z)(\eta-w))\). More general analytic polyhedra are relatively compact sets defined by finitely many holomorphic inequalities. Two defining functions are genuine global coordinates only with an injective biholomorphic change of variables; otherwise multiplicities matter.
reconstruction: Boundary regularity, holomorphy near closure and the coordinate-map caveat are supplied.
fate: The product formula is classical, and the polyhedral extension is explained in the pre-seminar work \citet[\S17 and Corollary~18.2]{norguet1961formes}. The notes are expository at this stage.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Hefer holomorphic difference decomposition
notes: The displayed lemma expresses \(f(z,w)-f(\zeta,\eta)\) as \((z-\zeta)P+(w-\eta)Q\), with holomorphic coefficients.
statement: If \(D\subset\mathbb C^n\) is a domain of holomorphy and \(f\in\mathcal O(D)\), there exist \(H_j\in\mathcal O(D\times D)\) such that \(f(z)-f(\zeta)=\sum_j(z_j-\zeta_j)H_j(z,\zeta)\). On a convex domain one may take \(H_j=\int_0^1\partial_j f(\zeta+t(z-\zeta))\,dt\); the global Stein-domain statement uses holomorphic division along the diagonal.
reconstruction: The domain-of-holomorphy hypothesis is essential to the global assertion. The convex-domain integral is a transparent special-case realization.
fate: \citet{hefer1950zerlegung} published the decomposition in 1950. The use and existence of these coefficients for domains of holomorphy are also stated in the opened \citet[p.~78, following Corollary~18.2]{norguet1961formes}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Cauchy--Weil representation on the distinguished boundary
notes: The notes sum over pairs of boundary faces, with a determinant of Hefer coefficients divided by two defining-function differences. The indices in the written kernel are incomplete.
statement: For a relatively compact analytic polyhedron \(P=\{|\chi_j|<1\}\subset D\subset\mathbb C^2\), with regular transverse boundary faces and \(D\) a domain of holomorphy, choose \(\chi_i(\zeta)-\chi_i(z)=\sum_{a=1}^2(\zeta_a-z_a)H_{ia}(\zeta,z)\). With the standard induced orientations on \(\Gamma_{ij}=\{|\chi_i|=|\chi_j|=1\}\cap\overline P\), a function holomorphic near \(\overline P\) has the Cauchy--Weil representation \((2\pi i)^{-2}\sum_{i<j}\int_{\Gamma_{ij}} f(\zeta)\det(H_{ia},H_{ja})\,d\zeta_1\wedge d\zeta_2/((\chi_i(\zeta)-\chi_i(z))(\chi_j(\zeta)-\chi_j(z)))\).
reconstruction: The determinant notation means the determinant of the two rows \((H_{i1},H_{i2})\), \((H_{j1},H_{j2})\); regularity and orientation are supplied. This is not a literal reproduction of the notebook\textquotesingle s mixed indices.
fate: The exact architecture of this kernel is already in \citet[\S17; Corollary~18.2]{norguet1961formes}, following Weil and Hefer. The construction is known before the 1965 seminar.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Polyhedral approximation and decomposition by face integrals
notes: The notes say that domains of holomorphy can be approximated by Weil domains and that the formula decomposes a holomorphic function into terms extending to larger regions.
statement: In a Stein domain, holomorphically convex compact sets admit relatively compact analytic-polyhedron neighborhoods. In a Cauchy--Weil representation, each face integral is holomorphic in any parameter region on which its coefficient functions are holomorphic and its denominator stays nonzero uniformly on the integration cycle. This gives controlled local extension/decomposition; it does not imply that every holomorphic function extends beyond its domain of holomorphy.
reconstruction: The relevant compact-set and nonvanishing conditions are the precise reconstruction of the broad approximation sentence.
fate: The polyhedral and ideal-theoretic foundations precede the seminar \citep{cartan1950ideaux}; \citet[Corollary~18.2]{norguet1961formes} provides the representation used here. The separate extensions of summands must not be confused with extension of their total across every boundary point.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: A continuous family of Weil defining functions
notes: The finite \(\chi_i\) are replaced by \(\chi(\alpha,z,w)\); a kernel containing \(P_1\partial_\alpha P_2-P_2\partial_\alpha P_1\) is sketched.
statement: The fragment proposes a continuous-parameter analogue of the Cauchy--Weil sum. It does not fix the parameter cycle, differentiability in \(\alpha\), the integration manifold, denominator order or orientations needed for an integral representation theorem.
reconstruction: No missing denominator power or integration cycle is guessed.
fate: Integral formulas with continuously varying complex hyperplanes are part of Gindikin\textquotesingle s work, including \citet[formula~(2)]{gindikin1965radon}. That paper identifies the next, linear example; it does not justify every symbol in this more general unfinished kernel. Searches did not recover an exact formula with all the manuscript\textquotesingle s conventions.
present_status: As of November 2026: a recognizable method with an incomplete exact statement; no independent open problem is inferred.

title: Linear defining functions and the holomorphic Radon transform
notes: For linear \(\chi\), the notes connect the formulas with Radon transforms, particularly in a tube over a convex domain.
statement: Let \(T_\Omega=\mathbb R^n+i\Omega\), where \(\Omega\) is open convex and contains no affine line. Under the smooth strictly convex assumptions of the initial construction, take a holomorphic \(f\) with sufficient rapid decay in the real directions on each horizontal slice. Its integrals over real \((n-1)\)-planes in suitable complex hyperplanes form a holomorphic Radon transform, with inversion by the specified oriented boundary integral in Gindikin\textquotesingle s formula~(2). The result requires these geometric and decay conditions.
reconstruction: The precise tube, rapid-decay hypothesis and initial boundary assumptions come from the paper, not from the shorthand notes.
fate: This is an exact match to \citet[pp.~237--239, formula~(2)]{gindikin1965radon}.
