The printed footnote records an announcement to the Moscow Mathematical Society on 23 February 1965, before this April seminar; the publication appeared in 1965. The article also discusses how its initial boundary regularity can be relaxed.
present_status: As of November 2026: established published work, with pre-seminar circulation distinguished from publication.

title: Review of sites, fiber products and sheaf descent
notes: The opening diagrams repeat products over an object, pullback of a cover, and compatibility of sections on double overlaps.
statement: For a site presented by covering families and the required fiber products, a sheaf of abelian groups is a contravariant functor satisfying the equalizer condition for every covering. Products in the slice represent overlaps; the universal property fixes all restriction maps used in the Čech complex.
fate: This continues record~40 and follows the pre-seminar site formalism of SGA~4; see \citet[Exposé II]{sga4I1972} and \citet[Tags 00VH, 00VL]{stacks2026sites}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Čech cochains and the alternating differential
notes: The terms are products of sections on multiple intersections, with alternating restriction maps; the notes show the first degrees and \(d^2=0\).
statement: For a cover \(\mathcal U=(U_i\to X)\), set \(\check C^q(\mathcal U,F)=\prod_{i_0,\ldots,i_q}F(U_{i_0}\times_X\cdots\times_XU_{i_q})\). The differential is the alternating sum of pullbacks along omission maps. Simplicial identities imply \(d^2=0\), and \(\check H^0(\mathcal U,F)=F(X)\) for a sheaf.
fate: This is classical Čech theory in the language of sites. The explicit construction and extension to complexes are given in \citet[Tags 01FP and 01GZ]{stacks2026cohomology}; the site version was part of the 1963--64 SGA program \citep{sga4I1972}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Refinement maps and direct-limit Čech cohomology
notes: A refinement is assigned a map of cochain complexes; cohomology over all covers is then considered.
statement: A chosen refinement map induces a cochain map in the opposite direction on Čech complexes. Two choices subordinate to the same refinement induce chain-homotopic maps, hence the same cohomology map. For ordinary open covers, direct-limit Čech cohomology is \(\check H^q(X,F)=\varinjlim_\mathcal U\check H^q(\mathcal U,F)\). On a site, one must use a specified refinement category and smallness convention.
reconstruction: Independence of the chosen refinement and the size convention are supplied; the notes do not prove them.
fate: The refinement construction is explicitly checked in \citet[Tag 01FP, Refinements]{stacks2026cohomology}. Passing to hypercovers gives derived sheaf cohomology on sites \citep[Tag 01GZ, Theorem~25.10.1]{stacks2026cohomology}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The direct-limit explanation of Čech exactness is false
notes: The source suggests that a long exact sequence exists for each cover but can fail after the passage over refinements.
statement: Filtered colimits of abelian groups are exact, so a compatible filtered system of long exact sequences remains exact. The actual issue is earlier: an epimorphism of sheaves need not be surjective on sections of an overlap, so a short exact sequence of sheaves need not give a short exact sequence of fixed-cover Čech complexes. In higher degree, ordinary Čech cohomology on an arbitrary site need not equal derived sheaf cohomology.
reconstruction: This separates the faithful source error from the correct motivation for derived functors.
fate: The derived-functor remedy was available before this talk in \citet{grothendieck1957tohoku}. The precise hypercover comparison is \citet[Tag 01GZ, Theorem~25.10.1]{stacks2026cohomology}. Neither result supports blaming a filtered direct limit for loss of exactness.
present_status: As of November 2026: the exactness issue is settled under the stated category conventions; the manuscript explanation is false.

title: Abelian sheaves, presheaves and exactness
notes: The notes contrast a category of sheaves with one of presheaves and discuss failure of exactness for an inclusion or section functor. A subscript resembling \(p\) is not securely identified as a stalk.
statement: Abelian presheaves form an abelian category with kernels and cokernels computed objectwise. Abelian sheaves also form an abelian category; their kernels are computed as presheaf kernels, while cokernels are obtained by sheafifying presheaf cokernels. The inclusion into presheaves is left exact and generally not right exact. On a topological space, exactness of sheaves is tested on stalks.
reconstruction: The ambiguous subscript is left unresolved; the three functors---inclusion, sections and stalk---are distinguished.
fate: This is part of Grothendieck\textquotesingle s abelian-category foundation \citep{grothendieck1957tohoku}; site formulations appear in SGA~4 \citep[Exposé II]{sga4I1972}. The notebook must not be read as denying stalkwise exactness.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The ideal sheaf of two points on the projective line
notes: The example takes two points of \(\mathbb P^1\), functions vanishing there, and an exact sequence whose global sections are not right exact.
statement: For distinct \(p,q\in\mathbb P^1_\mathbb C\), let \(J=\mathcal I_{\{p,q\}}\cong\mathcal O(-2)\). The exact sequence \(0\to J\to\mathcal O\to\mathbb C_p\oplus\mathbb C_q\to0\) gives \(H^0(J)=0\), \(H^0(\mathcal O)=\mathbb C\), and the diagonal map \(\mathbb C\to\mathbb C^2\), which is not onto. Its cokernel is \(H^1(J)\cong\mathbb C\), since \(H^1(\mathcal O)=0\).
reconstruction: The points are assumed distinct and the ground field complex, matching the holomorphic formulation. The cohomology calculation completes the source\textquotesingle s example.
fate: The example concretely illustrates the derived-functor theory already established in \citet{grothendieck1957tohoku}. The line-bundle notation identifies the exact obstruction; it is not an open extension problem.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: An incomplete differential-form exact sequence
notes: A sequence beginning \(0\to C\to\Omega^0\to\Omega\to0\) is sketched without a secure definition of the final sheaf or differential.
statement: On a smooth manifold, \(0\to\underline{\mathbb C}\to\mathcal A^0\xrightarrow{d}\mathcal Z^1\to0\) is locally exact, where \(\mathcal Z^1\) is the sheaf of closed smooth one-forms. The complete de Rham resolution instead continues through \(\mathcal A^1,\mathcal A^2,\ldots\). Replacing \(\mathcal Z^1\) by all one-forms and ending with zero is false in dimension greater than one.
reconstruction: The smooth de Rham example is a possible precise repair, explicitly not a decipherment of the unspecified final symbol.
fate: The Poincaré-lemma/de Rham interpretation is standard pre-seminar material, but the notebook does not decide whether \(\Omega\) means closed forms, an image sheaf or something else. The exact sequence is therefore not identified beyond this possible reconstruction.
present_status: As of November 2026: the proposed reconstruction is classical; the literal abbreviated sequence remains underdetermined.

title: Derived functors of sections and cohomology presheaves
notes: The final paragraph proposes right-derived functors of a left-exact functor from sheaves to presheaves, using injective resolutions to recover the long exact sequence.
statement: For abelian sheaves on a site, choose an injective resolution \(F\to I^\bullet\). Then \(H^q(U,F)=H^q(I^\bullet(U))\), and \(U\mapsto H^q(U,F)\) is a cohomology presheaf. Global cohomology is the right-derived functor of \(\Gamma(X,-)\). A short exact sequence of sheaves yields the usual long exact cohomology sequence. The inclusion of sheaves into presheaves is a different left-exact functor, whose derived values encode these local section cohomologies.
reconstruction: Enough injectives, the precise functor and the distinction between a cohomology presheaf and a cohomology sheaf are stated explicitly.
fate: Grothendieck\textquotesingle s 1957 paper established this derived-functor organization before the talk \citep{grothendieck1957tohoku}. \citet[Tags 01FP and 01GZ]{stacks2026cohomology} makes clear how Čech and hypercover constructions compare with it.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The invariant-subspace problem on complex Hilbert space
notes: The notes explicitly require a closed invariant subspace different from zero and the whole complex Hilbert space. On P000088 this is reformulated as whether the lattice can consist only of \(\{0,H\}\).
statement: For every bounded linear operator \(T\) on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space \(H\), must there be a closed subspace \(M\) with \(0\ne M\ne H\) and \(TM\subseteq M\)? Equivalently, can every nonzero vector be cyclic for one such \(T\)?
fate: The 1964 de Branges--Rovnyak announcement was retracted in 1965, as explicitly identified by Rovnyak\textquotesingle s author bibliography \citep{debrangesrovnyak1964existence,debrangesrovnyak1965correction}. The primary preprint \citet[abstract and Introduction, pp.~1--2]{marcoux2026generators}, dated 21 August 2026, still calls the precisely scoped Hilbert problem unsolved. Targeted searches through 12 November found claimed solutions and partial results; no generally accepted general solution was verified. A claim in a preprint is not treated as an established theorem.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026: no generally accepted solution was verified in the literature checked. This qualified status concerns bounded operators on complex infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, not arbitrary Banach spaces or special classes.
worth: Yes, as the central recognized problem, but an unrestricted attack is far beyond a bounded chapter development. The tractable work here is confined to the precisely specified Bishop family and finite-orbit certificates.

title: Normal and self-adjoint operators have invariant subspaces
notes: The normal and Hermitian cases are described as known.
statement: Every normal bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space of dimension greater than one has a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace. A nontrivial spectral projection gives a reducing subspace; when the operator is scalar, any one-dimensional subspace suffices. Self-adjoint operators are included.
reconstruction: The dimension restriction and the scalar exceptional argument prevent the shorthand from being applied to a one-dimensional space.
fate: This is classical spectral theory, already treated as established background in the contemporary polynomially compact discussion \citep[p.~433]{halmos1966polynomial}. It does not require compactness or an eigenvalue in the nonscalar continuous-spectrum case.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Compact operators and the Aronszajn--Smith theorem
notes: Completely continuous operators are attributed to von Neumann, followed by Aronszajn and Smith.
statement: Every compact bounded linear operator on an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space has a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace. In particular this holds on complex Hilbert space; for finite dimension greater than one, ordinary eigenvector theory supplies the result.
fate: \citet{aronszajnsmith1954} published the Banach-space theorem in 1954. The later primary account \citet[Introduction]{chamizo2020bishop} explicitly records the earlier unpublished von Neumann Hilbert-space result. The accessible Aronszajn--Smith record verified publication metadata; the complete original proof was not read.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Subnormality and the unilateral shift
notes: Subnormal means having a normal extension on a larger Hilbert space. The unilateral shift becomes normal after negative-index basis vectors are added; finite-dimensional subnormal operators are normal.
statement: An operator \(T\in B(H)\) is subnormal if \(H\) is an invariant subspace of a Hilbert space \(K\) for a normal \(N\in B(K)\), and \(T=N|_H\). The unilateral shift on \(\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\) is the restriction of the bilateral unitary shift on \(\ell^2(\mathbb Z)\). Finite-dimensional subnormal operators are normal. Taking adjoints need not preserve subnormality.
reconstruction: Invariance of the embedded space is essential: a compression of a normal operator to an arbitrary subspace would not be the stated notion.
fate: This is the established Halmos--Bram theory. The definition and intrinsic positivity criteria are recalled and extended by \citet[p.~99]{lambert1984subnormal}; Bram\textquotesingle s original 1955 paper is identified in its bibliography \citep{bram1955subnormal}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Invariant subspaces for subnormal operators
notes: After defining subnormality, the notes say that its invariant-subspace question is still unsolved.
statement: Does every subnormal bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space of dimension greater than one possess a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace? The answer is affirmative.
fate: \citet[abstract and pp.~310--333]{brown1978subnormal} proved the affirmative result, published in September 1978 after receipt on 21 July 1978. The publisher abstract was opened and explicitly states this result; the full subscription article was not read. The 1965 unsolved label is historically appropriate but cannot be retained as a current status.
present_status: As of November 2026: solved affirmatively by Brown in 1978; this special-class problem is distinct from item 1964-50.1.

title: Hyponormality is necessary but not sufficient for subnormality
notes: The overwritten qualification after \(T^*T-TT^*\ge0\) reads necessary and sufficient; the scan leaves the horizontal sign slightly ambiguous.
statement: Subnormality implies hyponormality \(T^*T-TT^*\ge0\), but the converse is false. The bounded unilateral shift with weights \(1,1,2,2,\ldots\) is hyponormal since the weights are nondecreasing. If it were subnormal, its moment measure would have moments \(\gamma_0=\gamma_1=\gamma_2=1\), forcing concentration at \(1\), contrary to \(\gamma_3=4\).
reconstruction: The minus sign is the mathematically coherent reading. The weighted-shift counterexample and moment argument are editorial verification; they are not attributed to the speaker.
fate: The full Bram--Halmos positivity conditions involve all finite arrays of vectors and powers, not just the first commutator; see \citet[Introduction and criterion]{lambert1984subnormal}. The recorded biconditional is a faithful mathematical error. The explicit shift supplies a short diagnostic counterexample, independently of the uncertain overwritten punctuation.
present_status: As of November 2026: the single positivity condition is insufficient; complete intrinsic subnormality criteria are established.

title: Polynomially compact operators have invariant subspaces
notes: The case \(T^2\) compact is attributed to Robinson and Bernstein using predicate calculus. Halmos then proves the general case \(p(T)\) compact for a nonzero polynomial.
statement: If \(H\) is an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, \(T\in B(H)\), and \(p\in\mathbb C[z]\setminus\{0\}\) has \(p(T)\) compact, then \(T\) has a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace. The case \(p(T)=0\) is included.
reconstruction: Infinite dimension and a nonzero polynomial are explicit. In finite dimension greater than one the conclusion is elementary; in dimension one it fails.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.1]{bernsteinrobinson1966} published the nonstandard-analysis proof in 1966; their paper was received 5 July 1964 and revised 10 December 1964. \citet[pp.~433--437]{halmos1966polynomial} gave the elementary proof, received 10 October 1964. Both manuscripts had been submitted before this May 1965 lecture, although publication followed it; the receipt dates alone do not establish public circulation. The coauthor is Allen R. Bernstein, not seminar participant I. N. Bernstein.
present_status: As of November 2026: established; the notebook is an early oral record of the subsequently published elementary proof.

title: Cyclic Hessenberg matrices and small subdiagonal products
notes: Gram--Schmidt on \(e,Te,T^2e,\ldots\) gives a matrix with one nonzero subdiagonal. Products along its lowest diagonal tend to zero by compactness of \(p(T)\).
statement: If one nonzero cyclic vector has linearly independent iterates, Gram--Schmidt gives \(a_{mn}=\langle Te_n,e_m\rangle=0\) for \(m>n+1\). For \(k\ge1\), \((T^k)_{n+k,n}=\prod_{j=1}^k a_{n+j,n+j-1}\). If \(p\) has degree \(k\), nonzero leading coefficient, and \(p(T)\) is compact, these products tend to zero, so some increasing subsequence of subdiagonal entries tends to zero.
reconstruction: The leading coefficient, consistent row-column convention and exceptional finite-dimensional orbit are made explicit.
fate: This is the reduction on \citet[pp.~433--434]{halmos1966polynomial}. A noncyclic orbit closure or a finite dependence already yields an invariant subspace. P000085 reverses the matrix indices in one definition; maintaining the convention from P000084 repairs the argument.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Almost invariant finite compressions and polynomials
notes: The small subdiagonal entry is used to compress \(T\) to initial finite-dimensional spans. Bounded vector sequences are compared modulo norm convergence to zero, with a special warning about constant terms.
statement: Let \(P_n\) be finite-rank orthogonal projections with \(P_n\to I\) strongly and \(\|(I-P_n)TP_n\|\to0\). For every polynomial \(p\) and bounded \(x_n\) with \(\|(I-P_n)x_n\|\to0\), one has \(\|p(T)x_n-p(P_nTP_n)x_n\|\to0\). On \(P_nH\), the compression admits a complete invariant flag.
reconstruction: The norm of the escaping corner, boundedness of the vector sequence, and asymptotic membership in \(P_nH\) are the exact sufficient hypotheses.
fate: The approximation lemma is in \citet[p.~435]{halmos1966polynomial}. The source\textquotesingle s two differently placed \(P_n\) factors explain its warning at exponent zero; dropping them silently would create a false formula for arbitrary bounded sequences.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Adjacent flags and weak limits in the compactness argument
notes: Two adjacent projections from each finite-dimensional invariant flag are chosen at a norm threshold. Their weak limits define spaces on which they converge strongly to the identity; compactness provides a nonzero limiting vector.
statement: For adjacent projections \(Q_n^-\le Q_n^+\), with rank-one difference and asymptotically invariant ranges, choose weak-operator limits \(Q^\pm\). The subspaces \(M^\pm=\ker(I-Q^\pm)=\{x:Q_n^\pm x\to x\}\) are closed and invariant. The compact polynomial and a correct threshold selection give \(M^-\ne H\), \(M^+\ne0\); rank-one adjacency excludes \(M^-=0\) and \(M^+=H\) simultaneously.
reconstruction: The weak limits are positive contractions. The mathematical mechanism is reconstructed from the exact publication; no unrecorded monotonicity of the displayed norms is assumed.
fate: This is the closing argument of \citet[pp.~435--437]{halmos1966polynomial}. Weak limits of projections need not be projections. The notebook\textquotesingle s missing terminal vector and conflicting threshold directions are not reproduced as a proof; the published selection supplies their precise repair.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: An entire function giving a compact operator reduces to a polynomial
notes: The notes state that if \(p\) is entire and \(p(T)\) compact, the polynomial result immediately gives an invariant subspace.
statement: Let \(f\) be a nonzero entire function and \(T\in B(H)\) on an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. If \(f(T)\) is compact, factor the finitely many zeros in a compact neighborhood of \(\sigma(T)\): \(f=p g\), where \(p\) is polynomial and \(g(T)\) is invertible. Then \(p(T)=g(T)^{-1}f(T)\) is compact, so the polynomial theorem applies.
reconstruction: The finite-zero factorization takes place near the compact spectrum, not over all of \(\mathbb C\). The analytic functional calculus supplies invertibility of the zero-free factor.
fate: This functional-calculus consequence uses the theorem of \citet{bernsteinrobinson1966,halmos1966polynomial}. The zero entire function must be excluded: allowing it would make the assumption hold for every bounded operator and simply restate the unsolved general problem.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The de Branges--Rovnyak compact-defect assertion
notes: After noting the error in their general announcement, the manuscript claims a consequence under \(\|T\|<1\) or \(\|T\|\le1\) and compact \(I-T^*T\). The scan does not securely distinguish the two norm signs.
statement: If \(\|T\|<1\), then \(I-T^*T\ge(1-\|T\|^2)I\); on infinite-dimensional \(H\), this operator cannot be compact. The strict reading is vacuous. The weak reading is a materially different assertion about a contraction with compact defect and requires a separate theorem; it is not certified by the retracted general proof.
reconstruction: The coercivity argument diagnoses the strict reading without choosing an uncertain glyph. No current open problem is manufactured from the weak reading.
fate: Rovnyak\textquotesingle s author bibliography identifies the 1964 announcement and its 1965 retraction \citep{debrangesrovnyak1964existence,debrangesrovnyak1965correction}. It does not verify the exact compact-defect corollary. The general retraction and the unresolved norm sign are kept separate.
present_status: As of November 2026: the strict hypothesis is impossible in the intended infinite-dimensional setting; an exact source for the non-strict compact-defect assertion was not verified.

title: Trace-class imaginary parts and triangular models
notes: Sakhnovich, Livshits and Brodskii are named for \(A+iB\), with \(A\) self-adjoint and \(B\) small in some sense, for example nuclear.
statement: One precise realization is the following. Let \(T=A+iB\) be bounded on a separable complex Hilbert space, with \(A=A^*\), \(B=B^*\), and \(B\) trace class. The restriction of \(T\) to the orthogonal complement of its maximal reducing self-adjoint part is unitarily equivalent to the corresponding non-self-adjoint part of a Liv\v{s}ic triangular model. The additional reducing component is self-adjoint. Here nuclear means trace class; small operator norm is not a substitute for this hypothesis.
reconstruction: The bounded separable Hilbert-space setting and the canonical self-adjoint real and imaginary parts are supplied explicitly. The nuclear example in the source identifies this established theorem, but its unspecified additional classes are not reconstructed. The stronger Hilbert--Schmidt criterion is reported by a later survey; its attribution was not independently confirmed in the cited 1959 original.
fate: \citet[Introduction, p.~145; \S11, Theorem~4, pp.~180--181]{livsic1954spectral} gives the triangular-model theorem for trace-class imaginary part. Its introduction dates the preliminary announcements to two 1952 notes. \citet[Introduction and theorem, pp.~180--181]{sakhnovich1959triangular} recalls this nuclear case and constructs a triangular representation under an explicit invariant-subspace interpolation condition. The latter paper was received 6 December 1957 and published in 1959. The broader survey discussion \citep[\S7, pp.~57--59]{dymkatsnelson2007schur} is kept distinct from the original results actually read.
present_status: As of November 2026: the nuclear example is an established pre-seminar result. The match is partial because the notebook does not identify its further small-imaginary-part classes or a particular theorem of each named author.

title: Contractions with neither forward nor adjoint powers strongly stable
notes: Both arrows in \(T^n\not\to0\), \((T^*)^n\not\to0\) are crossed; the norm condition is \(\|T\|\le1\). The result is attributed to Nagy and Foias.
statement: If \(T\) is a contraction on a complex Hilbert space with \(\dim H>1\), and neither \(T^n\) nor \((T^*)^n\) converges strongly to zero, then \(T\) has a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace.
reconstruction: Strong nonconvergence means failure for at least one vector for each sequence; it does not require every vector to have a nonzero limiting norm.
fate: This is exactly \citet[\S6, Theorem~3 and Remark~(ii), p.~314]{sznagyfoias1964ix}; footnote~29 handles the unitary case and dimension restriction. The paper was received 1 May 1964 and published in 1964. Its 1965 correction explicitly says that the error in Proposition~5.4 does not affect this theorem or its proof \citep[p.~193]{sznagyfoias1965corrections}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Donoghue lattice of finite initial spans
notes: The lattice \(\{0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}\) is attributed to Donoghue (1957). The upper-diagonal weights begin \(1/2,1/4\), followed by an uncertain \(1/8\) or \(1/6\).
statement: On \(\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\), the backward weighted shift \(Be_0=0\), \(Be_n=2^{-n}e_{n-1}\) for \(n\ge1\) is compact and quasinilpotent, and its closed invariant subspaces are exactly \(0\), \(\operatorname{span}\{e_0,\ldots,e_{m-1}\}\) for \(m\ge1\), and the whole space.
reconstruction: The geometric weight sequence is a literature-supported interpretation, not a confident decipherment of its overwritten third entry. The endpoints are the zero and whole subspaces.
fate: \citet[Examples~1--2, pp.~1031--1033]{donoghue1957lattice} proves the forward-shift tail lattice and its adjoint version. A scalar multiple yields the notebook\textquotesingle s normalization. The 1957 date is correct; the paper was received 25 June 1956.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Weight conditions for the Donoghue invariant-subspace lattice
notes: The exact conditions on the superdiagonal numbers that give precisely the Donoghue chain are said to be unknown.
statement: For a bounded sequence of nonzero weights \((w_n)_{n\ge1}\), determine criteria expressed in the weights for the backward shift \(Be_n=w_ne_{n-1}\), \(Be_0=0\), to have only finite initial spans and the whole space as closed invariant subspaces. Equivalently its forward-shift adjoint must be unicellular, with only coordinate tails.
reconstruction: Nonzero bounded weights and the Hilbert adjoint equivalence supply a precise classification question. The broad request for conditions is not silently replaced by an unverified demand for a novel universal closed-form criterion.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1 and subsequent counterexamples]{nikolskii1967weighted} gives weight conditions and examples delimiting them. \citet[\S1; Lemmas~2.1--2.2]{harrison1971unicellularity} develops further criteria. The opened abstract of \citet{yakubovich1985weighted} proves that positive moduli monotonically decreasing to zero suffice on \(\ell^p\), \(1\le p<\infty\); Hilbert adjoints give the backward form. \citet[p.~232]{latapokhriyalsingh2023powers} also credits Nikol\textquotesingle skii\textquotesingle s 1967 and 1968 work with additional necessary and sufficient conditions. The 1968 original was verified only at metadata level \citep{nikolskii1968basicity}; its exact scope is not guessed.
present_status: As of November 2026: developed and answered in substantial verified weight classes. The generality of a complete explicit characterization for arbitrary bounded nonmonotone weights was not ascertained in this audit. That verification gap is not classified as an established open problem.

title: An invariant-subspace chain indexed by all integers
notes: The question whether there is an operator with the structure of all integers is followed by unknown.
statement: There is a bounded operator on \(\ell^2(\mathbb Z)\) with full invariant-subspace lattice \(\{0,H\}\cup\{M_m:m\in\mathbb Z\}\), where \(M_m=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{e_j:j\ge -m\}\). In particular take \(Se_j=\exp(-2|2j+1|)e_{j+1}\). The \(M_m\) increase strictly, have intersection zero and dense union. The literal ordered set \(\mathbb Z\) needs the endpoints \(0,H\).
reconstruction: The endpoints and reversal of indexing are editorial. The concrete choice of Domar\textquotesingle s weights and the unitary conversion were checked independently in this audit; no novelty is claimed.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2, pp.~134--135; definitions p.~133]{domar1981translation} supplies an exact construction through weighted translation. Set \(w_n=\exp(-2n|n|)\). Then \(\log w\) is convex for \(n\le0\), concave for \(n\ge0\), \(\sum_{n\ne0}w_n^{1/n}=2\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-2n}<\infty\), and its quadratic limits are \(2>\log3\) at minus infinity and \(-2<-\log3\) at plus infinity. The unitary map \(c\mapsto(w_nc_n)\) turns right translation into the displayed shift. Domar proves that all invariant subspaces are the standard tails. Received 9 June 1980; published 1981.
present_status: As of November 2026: the completed integer-chain existence question is solved affirmatively by the established bilateral weighted-shift construction. The literal omission of least and greatest lattice elements is only a shorthand defect.

title: Volterra integration and a continuous chain
notes: The interval \([0,1]\) is represented by \((Vf)(x)=\int_0^x f(y)\,dy\), with the result dated to the 1950s.
statement: On \(L^2(0,1)\), the nonzero proper closed invariant subspaces of the Volterra operator are precisely \(M_a=\{f:f=0\ \text{a.e. on }(0,a)\}\), \(0<a<1\). With \(M_0=H\), \(M_1=0\), these form a continuous totally ordered lattice, reverse-ordered by \(a\), hence order-isomorphic to \([0,1]\).
reconstruction: The direction of inclusion and the endpoint subspaces are supplied; the Hilbert case is \(p=2\).
fate: \citet[Example~3, pp.~1033--1034]{donoghue1957lattice} gives the theorem and proof, including \(L^p\), \(1\le p<\infty\), and an appropriate continuous-function version. The existence assertion was established well before the seminar.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: A measure-Volterra lattice is not determined by the support as written
notes: A measure on the whole real line is drawn, \((Af)(x)=\int_0^x f(y)\,d\mu(y)\), and the lattice is conjectured to be isomorphic to \(\operatorname{supp}\mu\). The normalization resembles total mass one but is not secure.
statement: The literal conjecture is false even for an atomless probability measure: take \(d\mu=\tfrac12\mathbf1_{[-1,1]}dx\), interpreting the integral from zero in the oriented sense for negative \(x\). The subspaces supported on \([-1,0]\) and \([0,1]\) are closed, nonzero, proper and invariant, since every integration interval stays on its side of zero. They are incomparable, whereas \(\operatorname{supp}\mu=[-1,1]\) is linearly ordered.
reconstruction: The counterexample has no atoms, so endpoint conventions cannot explain away the failure. Its total mass is one. The boundedness of this particular integral operator follows directly from Cauchy--Schwarz.
fate: A repaired one-sided statement is classical: a positive continuous probability density on \([a,b]\), with lower integration limit \(a\), is transformed by its cumulative distribution into ordinary Volterra integration. The latter lattice is given by \citet[Example~3]{donoghue1957lattice}. This does not validate the two-sided source formula, and no general unresolved measure classification is inferred from that false conjecture.
present_status: As of November 2026: false under the literal two-sided formulation; the indicated regular one-sided repair is established.

title: Bishop operators as possible invariant-subspace counterexamples
notes: The weighted composition operator is specialized to \(Tf(x)=x f(x+\alpha\bmod1)\), irrational \(\alpha\). It is proposed as having no invariant subspace, equivalently every vector cyclic.
statement: For irrational \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), let \(T_\alpha f(x)=x f(\{x+\alpha\})\) on complex \(L^2(0,1)\). Does every such operator have a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace? The source\textquotesingle s contrary suggestion is false for many parameters, but the universal affirmative question is a distinct remaining problem. The equivalence with cyclicity requires every nonzero vector, not the zero vector.
reconstruction: The universal affirmative invariant-subspace question is a modern reformulation. The source suggests a counterexample without precisely delimiting the parameter set; its statement that every vector is cyclic must in any case exclude the zero vector.
fate: Davie\textquotesingle s 1974 theorem covers non-Liouville parameters; \citet[Theorem~3.7]{chamizo2020bishop} extends this to convergent denominators satisfying \(\log q_{j+1}=O(q_j/(\log q_j)^3)\), and hence includes some Liouville numbers. The same paper proves biquasitriangularity and norm approximation by nilpotent operators, neither of which alone produces an invariant subspace. \citet[Introduction]{behani2023bishop} explicitly retains the all-irrational question.
present_status: As of November 2026: the checked established results cover the stated arithmetic class, not every irrational parameter. No established all-parameter resolution was verified; the original no-subspace suggestion is already disproved for non-Liouville parameters.
worth: Yes. Exact finite-rotation products and quantitative rational approximation give concrete test cases. An invariant-subspace proof for the exceptional arithmetic regime still requires an argument beyond the finite-orbit continuity developed here.

title: Cyclic vectors for irrational Bishop operators
notes: After conjecturing that every vector is cyclic, the speaker says that not even one cyclic vector is known.
statement: For each irrational \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), does there exist \(f\in L^2(0,1)\) with \(\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{T_\alpha^n f:n\ge0\}=L^2(0,1)\)? A stronger concrete question asks when the constant function \(1\) is cyclic. Existence of one cyclic vector is far weaker than every nonzero vector being cyclic.
fate: \citet[Theorems~4.4--4.5, 4.9 and 4.16]{behani2023bishop} establishes rational cyclicity, a co-meager set of cyclic irrational parameters, and sufficient continued-fraction conditions. The preprint circulated in July 2022 and the paper appeared in 2023. Its Question~5.4 asks for an explicit approximation threshold. The chapter gives a bounded rational-fibre certificate and continuity estimate, not an all-irrational proof. A 2026 preprint lead was inaccessible and is not used as an established result.
present_status: As of November 2026: cyclicity is established for a co-meager parameter set and explicit sufficient classes in the checked work; universal irrational cyclicity was not verified. The historical absence of any known vector is obsolete.
worth: Yes. Rational cyclicity, exact finite products and strong continuity reduce selected questions to finite polynomial approximations with controlled error. The chapter develops such certificates and states their remaining arithmetic and conditioning obstacles explicitly.

title: The unspecified Ornstein cyclicity example
notes: An operator on \(L^2(0,1)\) is attributed to Ornstein, with every vector in \(L^{2+\varepsilon}\) cyclic. A nonsingular transformation without invariant measure is mentioned, but no operator is written.
statement: At minimum the cyclicity assertion must concern nonzero vectors and specify whether \(\varepsilon>0\) is fixed or varies. The operator, weight, transformation, and intended class of invariant measures are absent. A nonsingular transformation alone does not specify a bounded weighted-composition operator with the asserted cyclicity.
fate: Targeted searches on Ornstein, cyclic vectors, \(L^{2+\varepsilon}\), nonsingular transformations and invariant measures did not produce an opened primary theorem with these exact hypotheses. This anecdote is not identified with unrelated Ornstein results in ergodic theory, and no claimed counterexample to the Hilbert invariant-subspace problem is extracted from it.
present_status: As of November 2026: insufficiently specified and not securely identified; retained with explicit search limits.

title: Why invariant subspaces, and what could replace them?
notes: Gelfand asks why invariant subspaces are needed and what could replace them.
statement: This is a methodological question about structural invariants and operator models, not a quantified mathematical conjecture. Spectral measures, characteristic functions, similarity invariants and invariant-subspace lattices answer different versions of it.
fate: The next intervention gives one concrete contemporary response through analytic characteristic functions. No solved/open status is meaningful for the unrestricted methodological question itself.
present_status: As of November 2026: historical methodological discussion, not an independently unresolved theorem.

title: Analytic characteristic functions and the contraction model
notes: An English-speaking visitor with an uncertain F-name describes an analytic contraction from \(E\) to \(E_*\), Hardy boundary functions and analogues of Jordan blocks. The final finite-dimensional affine-map sentence does not specify the equivalence relation.
statement: For a completely nonunitary contraction \(T\), its characteristic function \(\Theta_T(z):\mathcal D_T\to\mathcal D_{T^*}\) is analytic and contractive for \(|z|<1\). It determines \(T\) up to unitary equivalence, modulo constant unitary identifications of the defect spaces. The standard model uses \([H^2(\mathcal D_{T^*})\oplus\overline{\Delta L^2(\mathcal D_T)}]\ominus\{\Theta_T f\oplus\Delta f:f\in H^2(\mathcal D_T)\}\), with \(\Delta=(I-\Theta_T^*\Theta_T)^{1/2}\).
reconstruction: The missing upper Fourier-integral limit is \(2\pi\); the positive exponent \(e^{int}\), \(n\ge1\), correctly kills negative Fourier coefficients. Complete nonunitarity and the defect-space constraints are essential. The separate finite-dimensional affine-map/Jordan analogy remains underdetermined.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1, p.~50; Theorem~3, p.~58]{sznagyfoias1964viii} gives the model and complete unitary invariant; it was received April 1963, revised December 1963 and published in 1964. \citet[Theorem~1 and formulas (3.16)--(3.17), pp.~294--295]{sznagyfoias1964ix} gives the factorization/invariant-subspace correspondence. This is an exact mathematical match, but not independent proof of the visitor\textquotesingle s identity.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: Unidentified participant (possibly C. Foiaş)
